 }\n    }\n  ],\n  \"artifactProjections\": [\n    {\n      \"path\": \"fixtures/batch-06/arena-walkthrough/a/proposal.md\",\n      \"originalExternalPath\": \"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-evaluation-20261016/fixtures/batch-06/arena-walkthrough/a/proposal.md\",\n      \"sha256\": \"4e13a7b539a42c8c47a6892f4b958595c834131547758ca5eb979bda16666f1e\",\n      \"bytes\": 7313,\n      \"owners\": [\n        \"grades-native-06.json#6\"\n      ],\n      \"text\": \"# Cache ownership and teardown proposal\\n\\nRecommend synchronous invalidation, with teardown callbacks retaining the value they own. Add an entry handle returned by `put` so a consumer can remove only its own entry. A cache lookup is a point-in-time lookup, not a lifetime guarantee.\\n\\n## Observed failure\\n\\nThe supplied after-state deletes an entry synchronously. In `caller.mjs`, unmount calls `subscription.dispose()` and then `invalidate(key)`. The exact vendored disposer schedules `onDispose` with `queueMicrotask` and returns immediately. The callback therefore runs after deletion and `get(key).ready` dereferences undefined.\\n\\nI ran `bun arena-walkthrough/input/probe.mjs` against the supplied files. It exited 1 and printed:\\n\\n    teardown error: TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'get(key).ready')\\n\\nThe removed timer previously deferred deletion until after the disposal microtask. That ordering explains why this caller depended on the old behavior. I did not execute a restored before-state, so that comparison is based on source inspection. The local vendor file SHA256 matches `manifest.json`: `d33e8d36600ad5df008657e478e39f9100a347098b4176f37923e5056cb3427f`. This evidence concerns fixture-v1 only and establishes no public package behavior.\\n\\n## Proposed API contract\\n\\n| Operation | Contract |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `put(key, value)` | Replace the current lookup entry and return an owned entry handle. Each put creates a fresh identity, even for the same value. |\\n| `get(key)` | Return the current value or undefined. Missing entries are ordinary misses. The result grants no guarantee about later lookups. |\\n| `handle.value` | Retain the exact value passed to this put, independent of lookup replacement or invalidation. |\\n| `handle.invalidate()` | Immediately remove the lookup entry only if this handle is still current for its key. Return whether removal occurred. Repeated calls are harmless. |\\n| `invalidate(key)` | Immediately remove whatever entry currently occupies the key and return whether removal occurred. Reserve this operation for code intentionally invalidating the current entry regardless of owner. |\\n\\nThe cache owns lookup membership. The consumer owns its subscription and the value reference needed during teardown. Removing an entry does not dispose subscriptions or mutate the value. A handle retains its value while consumers retain the handle. This proposal assumes ordinary JavaScript values as in the fixture; resource disposal requires a separate contract.\\n\\nFor `mount`, retain the handle returned by `put`. The disposal callback reports `handle.value.ready` instead of performing `get(key).ready`. Unmount schedules disposal once and invalidates through that handle. Guard unmount so repeated calls cannot queue duplicate reports. The pinned disposer itself does not provide idempotence.\\n\\nThis also handles overlapping mounts using the same key. If mount A is replaced by mount B before A unmounts, A reports its own value and its handle cannot delete B. A raw key-based invalidation would still delete B after fixing the missing lookup alone.\\n\\nThe retained reference is not a deep snapshot. Mutations to that object remain visible. If consumers require the final value of another owner instead, that is a different requirement and needs an explicit handoff. The fixture supplies no such requirement.\\n\\n## Errors and completion\\n\\nDo not turn the failed lookup into an optional-chain expression. That would suppress the exception while changing the report from true to undefined.\\n\\nCache operations contain no user callbacks. A missing or replaced entry makes `handle.invalidate()` return false. Define this as a normal result, not an error. Value validation belongs with the caller that understands `ready`.\\n\\nA report callback can still throw. Under the supplied disposer, that exception escapes from a microtask; a try/catch around unmount cannot catch it. Catch and route report failures inside the deferred callback through the application's existing error policy, or explicitly document uncaught callback errors if that is the policy. Do not claim that unmount reports asynchronous errors synchronously.\\n\\nKeep unmount synchronous for this migration and document that it schedules teardown but does not signal its completion. The vendor supplies no completion promise. If a future consumer must await disposal, introduce an adapter that observes callback completion and rejection, then expose an explicit asynchronous teardown contract. Merely awaiting `dispose()` would not provide that guarantee.\\n\\n## Alternatives rejected\\n\\n| Alternative | Reason |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Restore timer deletion permanently | It repairs this exact ordering but makes membership depend on scheduling. A pending deletion can also remove a replacement written under the same key. |\\n| Delay deletion with `queueMicrotask` | It couples the cache to this disposer's current scheduling and does not protect later or nested asynchronous cleanup. |\\n| Capture only the value and keep key-based invalidation | It fixes the demonstrated exception with a small caller change, but an old mount can still invalidate a newer mount. Use it only as an explicitly limited interim patch. |\\n| Make the whole cache reference counted | It requires release discipline and leak handling that the supplied ordinary-value cache does not need. Retained handles already preserve the required callback value. |\\n| Make every invalidation asynchronous | It expands the migration and still needs a definition of whose cleanup has completed. The cache does not own these subscriptions. |\\n\\n## Migration and acceptance checks\\n\\nFirst introduce entry handles without changing existing timer behavior, then migrate `mount` to retained values and owner-specific invalidation. Audit every caller for teardown-time `get` and overlapping key ownership before switching key-based invalidation to synchronous deletion. Deprecate unsafe consumer use of `invalidate(key)`, while keeping its deliberate current-entry semantics clear for administrative callers. Version or announce the timing change if callers outside this fixture consume the API.\\n\\nBefore implementation ships, verify actual behavior with the pinned vendor: normal unmount reports true exactly once after lookup removal; repeated unmount queues no extra report; external invalidation does not break disposal; A replaced by B can unmount without deleting B; a stale handle cannot remove a later put of the same object; report failures follow the documented policy. Keep the existing probe as evidence of the original failure. These proposed contracts and checks have not been implemented or validated here.\\n\\n## Assignment evidence and limits\\n\\nCandidate assignment: `arena-a-v1`, retry 1. This artifact is proposal-only and contains no implementation. The supplied package freeze is `f4623636a287bea2aa79c4b2234a53d20a5f193c`. The supplied input manifest revision is SHA256 `7dcb94c57c4014015efe5ffdd3b5c78548bf2e13e4029c103b7b55165aee3c43`; the manifest hashing convention was not supplied, so I do not claim to have independently reproduced that aggregate digest. No task Git SHA is available. The full Git input-revision gate remains reduced and this proposal cannot establish a full Arena method pass. The coordinator owns comparison, judgment and integration.\\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"path\": \"fixtures/batch-06/arena-walkthrough/b/proposal.md\",\n      \"originalExternalPath\": \"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-evaluation-20261016/fixtures/batch-06/arena-walkthrough/b/proposal.md\",\n      \"sha256\": \"366442d900bfe138e26bdbf8f6a86617afbfab48d520ce674aa9031cfd5c815b\",\n      \"bytes\": 7541,\n      \"owners\": [\n        \"grades-native-06.json#6\"\n      ],\n      \"text\": \"# Cache API proposal\\n\\nKeep cache invalidation synchronous and make teardown read the entry owned by its mount. Return an entry handle from put so an old mount can remove only its own generation. This separates lookup visibility from consumer lifetime without depending on event-loop delays.\\n\\n## Confirmed failure\\n\\nThe after-state invalidate deletes the Map entry immediately. The exact vendored createDisposer queues its callback with queueMicrotask and returns no completion signal. The caller invokes dispose, deletes the entry, then the queued callback evaluates get(key).ready against undefined. The diff alone hides that dependency.\\n\\nI ran bun arena-walkthrough/input/probe.mjs against the supplied files. It exited 1 with: teardown error: TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating get(key).ready). The vendor SHA-256 matches manifest.json: d33e8d36600ad5df008657e478e39f9100a347098b4176f37923e5056cb3427f. This establishes behavior for the local fixture-v1 implementation only. It establishes no public dependency behavior.\\n\\nThe removed setTimeout would place deletion after the queued microtask for this teardown. That ordering follows from the supplied code; I did not run a before-state comparison. Restoring it would preserve this narrow ordering but leave ownership ambiguous.\\n\\n## Proposed contract\\n\\n| Operation | Contract |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| put(key, value) | Replace the lookup entry and return a handle for that exact generation. |\\n| get(key) | Return the current value, or undefined when absent. |\\n| handle.value | Retain the supplied value reference for this consumer, even after replacement or invalidation. |\\n| handle.invalidate() | Synchronously remove the key only if it still refers to this handle generation. Return whether removal occurred. Repeat calls are harmless. |\\n| invalidate(key) | Synchronously remove the current lookup entry. Reserve this for a caller explicitly authorized to invalidate whichever generation is current. Return whether removal occurred. |\\n\\nA handle needs a unique internal identity. Comparing value equality is insufficient because callers can put the same object twice. The cache owns discoverability through get. Consumers own references they retain. Removing a lookup entry does not destroy its value, cancel a subscription, or invalidate an existing handle. The cache never invokes vendor disposal or owns consumer resource cleanup.\\n\\nThe consumer migration is conceptual, not an implementation in this proposal:\\n\\n1. Mount saves the handle returned by put.\\n2. The disposal callback reports handle.value.ready rather than performing another lookup by key.\\n3. Unmount calls subscription.dispose and calls handle.invalidate in a finally block. A local closed flag makes unmount idempotent before either action starts.\\n\\nThe retained object preserves reads of that particular object, including its later mutations. It does not promise a frozen snapshot. If two mounts use the same key, the older mount still reports its own value and cannot delete the newer mount when it closes. Explicit key-wide invalidation hides the entry from future lookups while retained consumers can finish cleanup.\\n\\n## Errors and completion\\n\\nA missing get returns undefined. Code that requires an entry must check it or keep an owned handle. Invalidation of an absent or replaced entry returns false, without throwing.\\n\\nIf dispose throws synchronously, finally still attempts owned invalidation and the original exception propagates. The closed flag prevents repeated disposal on another unmount call. The vendor provides no retry contract, so automatic disposal retries would be unsafe.\\n\\nErrors thrown by report inside the queued callback remain asynchronous errors under the existing consumer contract. A synchronous try/catch around unmount cannot catch them. Handle retention removes the missing-entry error, but does not suppress application callback failures. If the product requires error delivery through a promise, add a separate explicit completion/error adapter and define its callback semantics. Do not claim the current dispose method is awaitable.\\n\\nUnmount completion means disposal was requested and lookup ownership was released. It does not mean the queued report completed. Consumers that need stronger completion must use the separate adapter. A retained handle can prolong object lifetime, so consumers should release their subscription and handle references once their lifecycle finishes.\\n\\n## Alternatives considered\\n\\n| Alternative | Reason rejected for this proposal |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Restore setTimeout deletion | Repairs this fixture ordering but delays lookup invalidation, and an old timer can delete a replacement entry. |\\n| Queue deletion in a microtask | Relies on this vendor callback queue order and still lets stale owners delete new generations. |\\n| Await subscription.dispose() | The supplied dispose returns undefined. Awaiting it establishes no general disposal completion contract. |\\n| Change get to return a placeholder | Conceals missing entries and changes the meaning of ready. |\\n| Retain only a captured value with the current key-based invalidate | Fixes the observed exception, but leaves overlapping mounts vulnerable to deleting a newer entry. |\\n| Add reference counts and acquire/release leases | Useful if cache entries own destructible shared resources. The supplied cache holds plain values, so a generation handle is sufficient. |\\n\\n## Migration and verification plan\\n\\nFirst inspect all callers before changing put return values or enforcing handle ownership. Existing callers that ignore the new return can continue, but every consumer with delayed teardown must migrate before relying on synchronous invalidation. Document the lookup and lifetime contracts next to the exports. Update mount to keep its handle and remove its teardown lookup. Keep key-wide invalidation explicit for administrative invalidation use cases.\\n\\nBefore shipping an implementation, run the supplied real dependency probe and verify it reports disposed ready: true, then teardown completed with exit 0. Add behavioral checks for repeated unmount, old-unmount-after-replacement, two puts of the same object, invalidation before disposal, and report errors. Verify that synchronous invalidation hides lookup state before the queued callback while the callback still reads its retained value. These are proposed checks, not completed implementation tests.\\n\\n## Assignment evidence and limits\\n\\nThis artifact belongs to assignment arena-b-v1, candidate role, retryCount 0. Its only output is arena-walkthrough/b/proposal.md. I read task.md and every supplied input file. No implementation, external service, commit, installation, setting, or schedule was changed.\\n\\nThe coordinator supplied input manifest SHA-256 7dcb94c57c4014015efe5ffdd3b5c78548bf2e13e4029c103b7b55165aee3c43 and package freeze f4623636a287bea2aa79c4b2234a53d20a5f193c. The input task Git SHA is unavailable, so the full Git-revision assignment gate remains reduced. I have not substituted the package freeze for the task revision. The supplied manifest identifier is not the hash of the literal input/manifest.json file, whose observed SHA-256 is 5ed74232104c678e92d295f38648ee32dc80207816ed801ae845dbc80502fe29. I have not independently reconstructed the coordinator manifest algorithm.\\n\\nThe probe result and dependency hash above are observed command output. The proposed API and migration checks remain design work. No candidate comparison, independent judging, or full Arena completion is claimed by this artifact.\\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"path\": \"fixtures/batch-06/arena-walkthrough/checklist.md\",\n      \"originalExternalPath\": \"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-workflow-evaluation-20261016/fixtures/batch-06/arena-walkthrough/checklist.md\",\n      \"sha256\": \"5d87a149c9c9f496bca93211c6d84b9258c0b0df8d99baa9e3200fa317832554\",\n      \"bytes\": 211,\n      \"owners\": [\n        \"grades-native-06.json#6\"\n      ],\n      \"text\": \"- [x] Frame\\n- [ ] Fan out\\n- [ ] Cross-judge\\n- [ ] Pick\\n- [ ] Graft\\n- [ ] Verify\\nLocal checklist replaces unavailable todo operation. Return an identity-bound handle from put so an older consumer cannot remove a newer entry under the same key. The cache owns lookup membership. Each consumer owns its subscription and retained value.\\n\\n| Operation | Contract |\\n|---|---|\\n| put(key, value) | Replace lookup membership and return a fresh generation handle, even if the same value is inserted twice. |\\n| get(key) | Return the current value or undefined for a miss. |\\n| handle.value | Retain that generation's exact object reference, without promising a deep snapshot. |\\n| handle.invalidate() | Remove membership only if this generation is still current, returning whether removal occurred. |\\n| invalidate(key) | Remove whichever generation is current. Reserve for deliberate key-wide invalidation. |\\n\\nMount retains its handle. Its deferred callback reads handle.value.ready. Unmount marks itself closed before requesting disposal, then invalidates its own handle in finally. Repeated unmount does nothing. A synchronous disposal error propagates after owned invalidation. Asynchronous report errors follow an explicit application policy inside the deferred callback. The synchronous unmount return means teardown was requested, not that its callback finished.\\n\\nThe vendored dispose queues a microtask and returns undefined. Awaiting that return does not establish callback completion. The after-state probe throws because deletion precedes the deferred get(key).ready. Retention removes that dependency. Optional chaining would hide the broken contract and change the report value.\\n\\nIntroduce handles, migrate consumers, audit teardown-time lookups and overlapping mounts, then change existing key-wide invalidation timing. Publish or version this timing change only through a separately authorized delivery. No delivery occurred here.\\n\\nReject timer and microtask deferrals as a permanent lifetime contract. They couple correctness to scheduling and can remove replacement entries. Capturing only a value fixes the demonstrated exception but leaves stale key-wide deletion. Placeholder values hide missing data. Reference counting adds release and leak handling without evidence of destructible shared resources in this fixture.\\n\\nAn implementation must exercise successful deferred reporting after immediate lookup removal, repeated unmount, A replaced by B before A closes, two generations sharing one object, external invalidation before disposal, synchronous disposal errors and asynchronous report errors. Unmount's local invalidation has already completed before report runs.\\n\\nI rejected delayed invalidation with setTimeout. It depends on relative scheduler timing and leaves shared same-key ownership unresolved. I rejected a global map with generation tokens or reference counts because independent mounts do not need shared mutation. I also rejected disposal-completion-owned invalidation for this seat. That is a valid different design, but it extends cache lifetime and requires a completion contract absent from the pinned disposer. Seat B has no reason to read a cache during disposal once the value is explicit.\\n\\nI read all seven cache fixture files with git show at the specified input revision, including the actual vendored disposer and its manifest. The supplied disposer uses queueMicrotask, so synchronous invalidation removes the map entry before its callback reads get(key).ready. Its probe compares the imported file bytes against git show at the input revision and checks the manifest's SHA-256 before accepting the run. I corrected the observation method to capture the actual uncaught exception in a child; the implementation did not change. No remaining candidate check failures are known.\\n\\nFILE check-output.txt\\nPASS actual vendored disposer matches input revision and manifest digest\\nPASS cache invalidation is synchronous and repeatable\\nPASS deferred report reads captured value, double unmount reports once\\nPASS overlapping same-key mounts and remount before disposal stay independent\\nPASS report exceptions remain observable as uncaught deferred exceptions\\nAll 5 checks passed\\n\\nFILE caller.mjs\\nimport { createDisposer } from '../../../committed-inputs/additional/cache/vendor/disposer-v1.mjs';\\nimport { createCache } from './cache.mjs';\\n\\nfunction reportDisposed(value, report) {\\n  report(value.ready);\\n}\\n\\nexport function mount(key, report) {\\n  // The key identifies the mount to callers; mounts do not share storage by key.\\n  const cache = createCache({ ready: true });\\n  let mountedValue = cache.get();\\n  let unmounted = false;\\n  const subscription = createDisposer(() => {\\n    const value = mountedValue;\\n    mountedValue = undefined;\\n    reportDisposed(value, report);\\n  });\\n  return () => {\\n    if (unmounted) return;\\n    unmounted = true;\\n    try {\\n      subscription.dispose();\\n    } finally {\\n      cache.invalidate();\\n    }\\n  };\\n}\\n\\nFILE cache.mjs\\n// Each mount owns one cache cell. This review assesses selection and implementation quality; it assigns no case grade or host status. I inspected recorded execution results without rerunning the implementations.\\n\\n### arena-walkthrough\\n\\nSelecting A is supported by the actual code. Its entry retains the mounted value during disposal, then invalidates after reporting settles. Repeated teardown returns the same completion promise, and synchronous or asynchronous report failures reach the caller through rejection. B preserves the original value through a captured reference but invalidates before deferred reporting, which misses the literal temporal requirement. The judge explicitly recognized that distinction instead of treating both successful probes as equivalent evidence.\\n\\nThe synthesis coherently keeps A’s ownership and completion policy. The graft is a hand-adapted remount-before-disposal test from B; it does not introduce B’s immediate invalidation or uncaught microtask error policy. Rejecting a global map and timer-based deletion follows the demonstrated ownership and scheduling failure.\\n\\nVerification is substantive: the probe checks pinned vendor bytes against the committed input and digest, deferred execution, repeated teardown, independent same-key lifetimes, invalidation and failure handling. Both synthesis and graft verification records show exit `0`. These establish the exercised local behavior, not compatibility with an arbitrary disposer. A vendor that never calls back, or reporting that never settles, can retain the entry indefinitely. Callers must handle teardown rejection.\\n\\nThe native order supports a fresh later judge: B and A terminate at orders `25` and `26`, parent inspection follows at `29–30`, and the distinct judge starts at `31`. Judgment completes at `37`, before synthesis at `43`.\\n\\nThe exploration’s breadth is constrained: the coordinator assigned both whole shapes in advance. This is a comparison of those alternatives, not evidence that the workers independently discovered the design space.\\n\\n### candidate-cross-review\\n\\nThe selected A implementation directly satisfies the required lifecycle ordering. Its entry owns value retention, the actual deferred disposer and completion. The distinct-value overlap probe is particularly useful: it demonstrates separate ownership beyond two callbacks that both report `true`.\\n\\nB is meaningfully different from A and from walkthrough B: it retains an explicit caller-owned map with identity-guarded invalidation. That guard prevents an older mount from deleting a newer value, but does not restore an older active value after the newest mount unmounts. It also reports after invalidation and exposes more coordination surface. Those are concrete reasons to prefer A. The judge’s rejection of B’s immediate invalidation, map plumbing and uncaught report-error policy is consistent with the implementation.\\n\\nThe synthesis preserves A and grafts coverage of both same-key teardown orders plus remount-before-disposal. It avoids combining incompatible ownership policies. Recorded synthesis and graft probes exit `0`, including reproduction of the committed original failure, vendor pinning, asynchronous lifetime retention and cleanup after report errors.\\n\\nThe selected implementation assumes the pinned disposer’s scheduling behavior. Its `subscription.dispose()` call sits outside a scheduling-failure cleanup path; a synchronous scheduling exception would leave its completion unresolved. The supplied vendor normally queues a microtask, so the existing report-failure checks do not establish this additional behavior.\\n\\nThe separate trials are honestly bounded:\\n\\n- Native evidence records the unavailable-worker spawn rejection, `agent thread limit reached`. No worker artifact is substituted for that rejection.\\n- The dropout worker actually executes the authorized failure command and exits `7`. Its `failure.json` records no candidate and excludes integration. The worker completes its report while the task assignment remains blocked.\\n- The survivor contains a real lifecycle proposal, implementation, rationale and probe. Its parent-check record exits `0`. It remains one survivor, with no competitive selection, judge or trial synthesis claimed.\\n\\nMain candidates terminate at orders `50` and `54`; parent inspection occurs at `55–56`; the fresh judge starts at `57`, completes at `60`, and synthesis follows at `62`. The failure exercises remain separate from that main comparison.\\n\\n### boundary-design\\n\\nA is the better fit for the stipulated package.       "path": "fixtures/cases/arena-walkthrough/outputs/raw/exact-source-reads.json",
      "bytes": 7838,
      "sha256": "99ae5a845ca7d44ae68b9864536d9209416352179c2e2f5c0946b23c8b9393f5",
      "owner": "local-013-initial-arena-walkthrough",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "[\n  {\n    \"path\": \"/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/arena/SKILL.md\",\n    \"content\": \"---\\nname: arena\\ndescription: \\\"Spawn N parallel candidates at the same task, pick a base, graft the strongest parts of the losers into it. Use for /arena, 'arena this', 'throw it in the arena', or when one attempt at a non-trivial artifact would lock in the wrong shape.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Arena\\n\\nRead [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md), [assignment and integration](../../references/orchestration-contract.md), and [workflow ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md). Use only exposed, authorized operations. Read each applied principle leaf in full before dependent work. Missing required reads block that work. Invocation aliases are guidance, not proof of registered host commands.\\n\\nIndependent candidates and a fresh independent judge require observed worker operations and inspected artifacts. If unavailable, produce authorized sequential alternatives and parent comparison only as reduced capability. Do not claim independence, background execution, model diversity or a full arena pass. If independence is required, leave that gate blocked.\\n\\nFan out N parallel attempts at the same task. Read every candidate end to end. Pick the strongest as the base. Graft the best ideas from the others into it. Verify the synthesized result.\\n\\n## Start\\n\\nOpen an exposed todo list with one entry per phase before launching anything. Without one, use an authorized local Markdown checklist and disclose the reduced binding.\\n\\n1. Frame\\n2. Fan out\\n3. Cross-judge\\n4. Pick\\n5. Graft\\n6. Verify\\n\\n## Phase A: Frame\\n\\nThe N candidates will receive the same prompt, so the prompt is the contract.\\n\\n1. State the artifact each candidate is producing.\\n2. Derive the rubric. State what success looks like for *this* task, then turn it into 3-6 concrete gradeable criteria. The rubric is the picker's tool in Phase D. Candidates only see the task.\\n3. Pick the runners. Use an explicitly supplied, authorized `arena runners` preference if available. Otherwise request two inherited workers, one per seat. The source defaults used two specific model families. Their source-host slugs are not portable availability evidence. Select an explicit model or effort only from current exposed documentation or observed enumeration under the model-role contract. An `auto` or `inherit-parent` entry means omit explicit model selection. On rejection, record it and disclose a supported same-family alternative when available, otherwise an authorized inherited alternative. If the exact model is required, block instead. Record requested and observed model and effort separately, using unknown when unobserved. More seats can cover multiple design directions. Same model N times is appropriate when work is generation-bound rather than judgment-sensitive. Unknown models leave diversity unverified.\\n4. Assign output paths. Each candidate writes to its own authorized location, a git worktree where supported, otherwise a distinct local candidate directory. Follow [separate-before-serializing-shared-state](../principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state/SKILL.md). Confirm isolation and write permissions before dispatch. Record immutable assignment identity, input SHA, owner, role and evidence links under the assignment contract. Workers never integrate shared files. Worktree creation and persistence require observed authorized capabilities.\\n\\n## Phase B: Fan out\\n\\nDispatch all N independent candidates together through the exposed worker operation, using observed background execution when available. Give each the same task, shared grounding path, its isolated output path, and instructions to produce both the artifact and a short rationale. Withhold the rubric from candidates. Inspect terminal results and artifact paths before accepting completion; a wait notification alone is insufficient.\\n\\nEach rationale names the alternatives the candidate considered and what it rejected.\\n\\nIf a candidate fails to produce output, proceed with N-1 and note the dropout in the synthesis record. One survivor means incomplete competition, even if its artifact is useful. Zero survivors blocks synthesis. Never integrate partial or cancelled artifacts as completed candidates.\\n\\n## Phase C: Cross-judge\\n\\nAfter all Phase B candidates reach terminal state and their accepted artifacts are inspected, choose one model from an explicitly supplied, authorized `arena cross-judge pool` preference. Without that preference, use an inherited worker or a supported explicit selection under the model-role contract. The source pool named the same two families as the runners; it does not establish portable model availability. Prefer a different observed model family from the parent's when available. Disclose rejected choices and supported fallbacks, or block if the exact choice is required.\\n\\nSpawn one fresh readonly judge worker. It sees the rubric and completed candidates by path label, scores each criterion, and recommends a base with rationale. It runs in parallel with the parent's reading in Phase D when observed background execution permits it, never with candidates still writing. The judge has no candidate write ownership. Unknown actual models leave diversity unverified. Unavailable fresh judging remains a reduced or blocked gate, never an invented independent verdict.\\n\\n## Phase D: Pick a base\\n\\nRead every candidate end to end before picking.\\n\\nScore each candidate against the rubric criterion by criterion, not on holistic feel. Compare against the cross-judge. Agreement on the base confirms the pick. Disagreement means one of you is biased or the rubric was ambiguous. Read both rationales before deciding.\\n\\nPick the base on which candidate a future maintainer can extend most easily without breaking invariants. Prefer the cleaner boundary or smaller API when two feel tied, per the [Laziness Protocol](../principle-laziness-protocol/SKILL.md).\\n\\nRecord the pick and the reason in a short synthesis note alongside the base artifact, including the cross-judge's verdict.\\n\\n## Phase E: Graft\\n\\nWalk each losing candidate once more and identify what is worth porting into the base. The signal is usually one or two things per candidate, not most of it.\\n\\nFold each graft in by hand, per [redesign-from-first-principles](../principle-redesign-from-first-principles/SKILL.md). Don't paste mechanically. The result has to remain coherent under one mental model.\\n\\nRecord what was grafted, from which candidate, and what was rejected and why.\\n\\nWhen N candidates converge on the same shape, that is a strong agreement signal. Note the convergence in the record and deliver the consensus shape within authorized scope. No graft is needed. When N candidates wildly diverge, Phase A was under-specified. Reframe and re-run rather than averaging the divergence.\\n\\n## Phase F: Verify\\n\\nThe synthesized artifact has to hold up under the same scrutiny as any other output, per [prove-it-works](../principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md).\\n\\nIf verification surfaces a problem the arena did not catch, either Phase A was wrong (re-frame and re-run) or one candidate caught it and you missed the graft (go back to Phase E). Don't paper over.\\n\\nApply [unslop](../unslop/SKILL.md) to the synthesis prose. External publication, commits, messages and setup require their own authorization.\\n\\n## Outputs\\n\\nOne synthesized artifact. One short synthesis note alongside, naming the base, the grafts and their source candidates, the rejections, the dropouts if any, and the verification result.\\n\",\n    \"bytes\": 7536\n  }\n]"

      "text": "import { createDisposer } from '../fixture/vendor/disposer-v1.mjs';\n\n// Each factory call owns its lookup and all mount lifecycles.\nexport function createLifecycleCache() {\n  const entries = new Map();\n  function mount(key, report, value = { ready: true }) {\n    const entry = { value };\n    entries.set(key, entry);\n    let completion;\n    let resolveCompletion;\n    let rejectCompletion;\n    const subscription = createDisposer(async () => {\n      try {\n        await report(entry.value.ready);\n        resolveCompletion();\n      } catch (error) {\n        rejectCompletion(error);\n      } finally {\n        // An older lifecycle must never invalidate its replacement.\n        if (entries.get(key) === entry) entries.delete(key);\n        entry.value = undefined;\n      }\n    });\n    return function unmount() {\n      if (completion) return completion;\n      completion = new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n        resolveCompletion = resolve;\n        rejectCompletion = reject;\n      });\n      subscription.dispose();\n      return completion;\n    };\n  }\n  return { mount, get: key => entries.get(key)?.value };\n}\n"
    },

      "text": "import assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { createHash } from 'node:crypto';\nimport { createLifecycleCache } from './implementation.mjs';\nconst vendor = await Bun.file(new URL('../fixture/vendor/disposer-v1.mjs', import.meta.url)).arrayBuffer();\nassert.equal(createHash('sha256').update(new Uint8Array(vendor)).digest('hex'), 'd33e8d36600ad5df008657e478e39f9100a347098b4176f37923e5056cb3427f');\nconst a = createLifecycleCache();\nconst b = createLifecycleCache();\nconst seen = [];\nconst old = a.mount('k', ready => seen.push(['old', ready]), { ready: 'old' });\nconst newer = a.mount('k', ready => seen.push(['new', ready]), { ready: 'new' });\nconst isolated = b.mount('k', ready => seen.push(['isolated', ready]), { ready: 'isolated' });\nconst pending = old();\nassert.equal(old(), pending);\nassert.deepEqual(seen, []);\nawait pending;\nassert.deepEqual(seen, [['old', 'old']]);\nassert.equal(a.get('k').ready, 'new');\nassert.equal(b.get('k').ready, 'isolated');\nawait newer();\nassert.equal(a.get('k'), undefined);\nawait isolated();\nassert.equal(b.get('k'), undefined);\n// Reverse unmount order also preserves each mount's own value.\nconst reverse = [];\nconst first = a.mount('reverse', x => reverse.push(x), { ready: 1 });\nconst second = a.mount('reverse', x => reverse.push(x), { ready: 2 });\nawait second();\nawait first();\nassert.deepEqual(reverse, [2, 1]);\nlet release;\nconst gate = new Promise(resolve => { release = resolve; });\nconst held = { ready: 'retained' };\nconst unmountHeld = a.mount('held', async ready => {\n  assert.equal(ready, 'retained');\n  await gate;\n  assert.equal(a.get('held'), held);\n}, held);\nconst heldDone = unmountHeld();\nawait Promise.resolve();\nassert.equal(a.get('held'), held);\nrelease();\nawait heldDone;\nassert.equal(a.get('held'), undefined);\nfor (const report of [() => { throw new Error('sync failure'); }, async () => { throw new Error('async failure'); }]) {\n  const fail = a.mount('failure', report);\n  const done = fail();\n  await assert.rejects(done, /failure/);\n  assert.equal(a.get('failure'), undefined);\n  assert.equal(fail(), done);\n}\nconsole.log('PASS: pinned vendor; deferred own-value reads; replacement safety in both orders; isolated instances; idempotent unmount; asynchronous retention; failure cleanup and propagation.');\n\n// Graft from candidate B: remount after teardown is scheduled, before its callback.\nconst interleaved = createLifecycleCache();\nconst records = [];\nconst stopOld = interleaved.mount(\"interleaved\", ready => records.push(ready), {ready:\"original\"});\nconst oldDone = stopOld();\nconst stopNew = interleaved.mount(\"interleaved\", ready => records.push(ready), {ready:\"replacement\"});\nawait oldDone;\nassert.deepEqual(records,[\"original\"]);\nassert.equal(interleaved.get(\"interleaved\").ready,\"replacement\");\nawait stopNew();\nassert.deepEqual(records,[\"original\",\"replacement\"]);\nassert.equal(interleaved.get(\"interleaved\"),undefined);\nconsole.log(\"PASS: grafted remount-before-callback scenario\");\n"

    {
      "path": "fixtures/cases/arena-walkthrough/outputs/working/candidate-a/proposal.md",
      "bytes": 2705,
      "sha256": "68da070d7b6aa0004e9e9c94ef920dc742eb70299b86b9f3be026373fc08eab3",

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "# Lifecycle-owned cache entries\n\nAssignment: arena-candidate-a. Method: arena.\nInput revision: 5453137ccc4e5d1f0b78726eabd8d13295ba0468.\n\nThe supplied caller synchronously deletes its key immediately after asking the pinned disposer to enqueue a microtask. The callback later evaluates `get(key).ready` against an empty map and throws. The removed timer used to delay deletion beyond the microtask, but timing is not ownership.\n\n`createLifecycleCache()` owns one lookup map per instance. Each mount allocates an entry object and closes its deferred callback over that entry. That entry retains its mounted value through completion of the report, including an asynchronous report. Lookup replacement changes which entry is discoverable; it does not transfer ownership of an old lifecycle's mounted value.\n\nUnmount returns a shared completion promise and schedules the exact imported vendor disposer once. Repeated unmount returns that same promise, including after failure. Cleanup runs in `finally`, clears the lifecycle's value, and only deletes the map key if the map still points to that entry. An older mount therefore cannot delete a newer mount at the same key. Each mount reports its own value in either unmount order. Failed reports reject the completion promise after cleanup; callers must await or otherwise handle that promise. There is no retry after failure. A never-settling report intentionally retains its value and key; timeout or cancellation policy belongs to the caller.\n\nUsage:\n\n```js\nconst cache = createLifecycleCache();\nconst unmount = cache.mount('fixture-key', ready => console.log(ready));\nawait unmount();\n```\n\nThe cached object is retained by reference, matching normal cache behavior; this does not provide immutable snapshots against external mutation. New same-key mounts supersede lookup visibility. Unmounting the newest mount does not restore an older mount to lookup, though that older lifecycle can still dispose safely.\n\nRejected alternatives: a global mutable map shares ownership across consumers; timer-based invalidation relies on event-loop ordering and still permits same-key collisions; deleting by key without entry identity lets old cleanup remove replacements. Capturing only a raw value is a valid alternative design, but this assignment uses a lifecycle entry so retained data and teardown state share one owner.\n\nVerification uses the actual vendored implementation, checks its manifest SHA-256, and covers independent instances, deferred reads, both same-key unmount orders, repeated unmount, pending asynchronous reporting, and synchronous/asynchronous failure. This establishes behavior only for the supplied local dependency, not any public package.\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "fixtures/cases/arena-walkthrough/outputs/working/candidate-b/proposal.md",
      "bytes": 2879,
      "sha256": "ebb037e546c8b87c14b10f00603646d6bea23b569d6eae12662ed25780e04422",
      "owner": "local-013-initial-arena-walkthrough",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "# Explicit captured-value disposal\n\nAssignment: arena-candidate-b. Method: arena. Input revision: 5453137ccc4e5d1f0b78726eabd8d13295ba0468.\n\nThe supplied synchronous invalidation removes the map entry before the vendored disposer's queued microtask reads it. Running the supplied probe with Bun exits 1 with a TypeError at `get(key).ready`. The exact local dependency queues the callback; it does not synchronously execute it.\n\nGive every mount its own cache owner. Pass the mounted value explicitly to `capturedDisposal(value, report)` during mount. Its deferred callback reads that captured value directly. Unmount marks itself completed, schedules disposal, and synchronously invalidates only its own slot. Neither the cache nor the deferred callback looks up a global mutable map.\n\nTwo mounts with the same key retain independent slots and captured values. An old unmount cannot erase a newer mount. Repeated unmount is a no-op, even before the first callback runs. Mount's existing return-a-function calling convention remains usable. The optional third argument permits distinct fixture values without changing existing callers.\n\nInvalidation removes the owner's reference immediately; the disposal closure retains the mounted object until the callback completes. This captures object identity, not a deep snapshot: external mutation of that object remains visible. The report receives `ready`, preserving the supplied caller's behavior. Values must have the supplied fixture shape; this proposal does not add validation or persistence semantics.\n\nThe unmounted flag is set before scheduling and is never reset. A scheduling failure still invalidates the owner through `finally`, surfaces synchronously, and is not retried. With the pinned vendor, scheduling uses `queueMicrotask`. Report failure surfaces as an uncaught deferred error, cannot be caught around unmount, and is not retried. The capture is released in `finally` even when reporting throws. This preserves ordinary error propagation without silently swallowing failures.\n\nRejected alternatives: delaying invalidation with a timer restores ordering but leaves shared-key ownership collisions and depends on scheduling; switching to a different disposer invents dependency behavior; a global key-to-value lookup can observe another mount or no entry; lifecycle-owned callback reads are a viable distinct design but this assignment specifically chooses an explicit value argument. No changes to the exact vendored disposer are needed.\n\nThe implementation imports the supplied pinned vendor verbatim. Verification checks its SHA-256, immediate local invalidation, deferred timing, overlapping mounts with different values at the same key, remount before callbacks, duplicate unmount, and report failure in an isolated child process. The result applies only to this local fixture dependency, not a public package.\n"

Requested model/effort inherit-parent; actual model/effort unknown.\n\nThe fresh judge recommends candidate B, 10/10, ahead of A, 9/10. Both implement their assigned shapes. B preserves useful key-based cache lookup with explicit ownership; A removes shared lookup semantics.\n\n| Rubric criterion | A | B |\n| --- | ---: | ---: |\n| Deferred teardown reads its own value before invalidation | 2 | 2 |\n| Explicit local ownership and same-key isolation | 2 | 2 |\n| Repeat disposal and failure semantics | 2 | 2 |\n| Caller API and extension cost | 1 | 2 |\n| Runnable implementation and actual Bun checks | 2 | 2 |\n\nA's entry design is compact, but restoring key retrieval requires a separate registry and collision policy. B's local map and ownership tokens preserve lookup with a small mechanism.\n\nGraft A's single finally cleanup path. Keep B's captured value and token-conditional invalidation. Do not combine both ownership abstractions or restore timers, global state, unconditional deletion, late key lookup, or swallowed errors. Adopt a complete artifact inventory and documented hash scheme.\n\nJudge identified that B's unmount closure retains its captured value after completion. Invalidation alone does not prove object reclamation. Both retain values indefinitely for callbacks that never settle, and self-await deadlocks. B assumes its own cache methods; arbitrary throwing invalidation could otherwise leave completion unresolved. Replace inherited implementation README text and label the historical diff.\n\nThe judge observed 13 passing candidate tests, 53 assertions, and both probes exiting 0. No files were written by the judge. The artifact generator was not run because it writes metadata.       "text": "# Candidate B: explicit captured disposal value\n\nAssignment: arena-candidate-b. Seat: candidate-b. Owner: /root/candidate_b.\nMethod: arena. Input revision: 5453137ccc4e5d1f0b78726eabd8d13295ba0468.\nRequested model/effort: inherit-parent. Actual model/effort: unknown.\n\n`input/` is the untouched selected fixture copy. `implementation/` contains the complete runnable solution and an unchanged pinned vendored disposer. The old README and invalidation.diff in that directory describe the original fixture only.\n\nThe cache is created per application with createCache(); mount(cache, key, report, value?) captures its exact value and passes it explicitly to disposeCaptured(value, report). Disposal does not retrieve data by key. unmount() returns a completion promise and schedules the supplied real microtask disposer once. Await that promise to observe completion or handle errors. Callback completion, including asynchronous work, precedes invalidation. Failure rejects the promise after cleanup. Repeated calls share the same promise and outcome.\n\nKeys have latest-write-wins visibility. A unique ownership token makes an older disposal unable to delete a replacement, including a replacement mounted inside its callback. Different caches have separate maps. A displaced mount still disposes its captured value. There is no shared global mutable cache.\n\nRejected alternatives: delaying deletion by a timer merely relies on scheduling and still reads replacements for duplicate keys. A global map leaks across owners. A lifecycle-owned entry was not implemented because this seat requires explicit captured disposal arguments. Capturing a key and looking it up later loses value identity. Unconditional deletion would remove newer ownership. Swallowing errors would make cleanup outcomes unobservable.\n\nTradeoffs: captured values are references, not immutable snapshots; caller mutations remain visible. Values remain reachable until asynchronous reports finish, and a report that never settles prevents completed cleanup. There is no timeout/cancellation policy in the fixture. Reentrant code must not await the same unmount promise from inside its own report. A caller must handle rejected unmount promises. The public API changes from implicit global access to explicit cache ownership.\n\nVerified with Bun 1.4.2:\n\n| Command | Exit | Result |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| bun test outputs/candidate-b/implementation/cache.test.mjs | 0 | 7 passed, 0 failed, 21 assertions |\n| bun outputs/candidate-b/implementation/probe.mjs | 0 | disposed ready: true; teardown completed |\n| bun outputs/candidate-b/input/probe.mjs | 1 | Original deferred-disposal race reproduced as TypeError |\n| git rev-parse HEAD && git diff --exit-code | 0 | Exact input SHA retained; committed inputs unchanged |\n\nRaw verification arguments and full returns are retained in raw-verification.json. No dependencies were installed, no external services accessed, and no commits created.\n"

    {
      "path": "reruns/local-01/arena-walkthrough/outputs/candidate-b/implementation/caller.mjs",
      "bytes": 828,
      "sha256": "349c9726ef448c3e242fec1248ef80f195e03eb23cc6fdfdb23f440e0b5175e6",
      "owner": "local-013-arena-walkthrough-early-repair",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import { createDisposer } from './vendor/disposer-v1.mjs';\nasync function disposeCaptured(value, report) {\n  await report(value.ready);\n}\nexport function mount(cache, key, report, value = { ready: true }) {\n  if (typeof report !== 'function') throw new TypeError('report must be a function');\n  const owner = cache.put(key, value);\n  let completion;\n  let resolve;\n  let reject;\n  const subscription = createDisposer(async () => {\n    try {\n      await disposeCaptured(value, report);\n      cache.invalidate(key, owner);\n      resolve();\n    } catch (error) {\n      cache.invalidate(key, owner);\n      reject(error);\n    }\n  });\n  return function unmount() {\n    if (!completion) {\n      completion = new Promise((ok, fail) => { resolve = ok; reject = fail; });\n      subscription.dispose();\n    }\n    return completion;\n  };\n}\n"
    },

    {
      "path": "reruns/local-01/arena-walkthrough/outputs/candidate-b/implementation/cache.test.mjs",

      "sha256": "09c06fa74f970119ac05d3ef2501d0972ef505ac188ce93ac2dfee8b87a10ccb",
      "owner": "local-013-arena-walkthrough-early-repair",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import { test, expect } from 'bun:test';\nimport { createCache } from './cache.mjs';\nimport { mount } from './caller.mjs';\n\ntest('deferred callback reads mounted value before invalidation', async () => {\n  const cache = createCache();\n  const value = { ready: true };\n  const seen = [];\n  const unmount = mount(cache, 'x', ready => { seen.push(ready); expect(cache.get('x')).toBe(value); }, value);\n  const done = unmount();\n  expect(seen).toEqual([]);\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBe(value);\n  await done;\n  expect(seen).toEqual([true]);\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBeUndefined();\n});\n\ntest('duplicate keys capture distinct values and preserve replacement', async () => {\n  const cache = createCache();\n  const seen = [];\n  const old = mount(cache, 'x', ready => seen.push(ready), { ready: 'old' });\n  const value = { ready: 'new' };\n  const latest = mount(cache, 'x', ready => seen.push(ready), value);\n  await old();\n  expect(seen).toEqual(['old']);\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBe(value);\n  await latest();\n  expect(seen).toEqual(['old', 'new']);\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBeUndefined();\n});\n\ntest('repeat disposal shares completion and reports once', async () => {\n  const cache = createCache();\n  let calls = 0;\n  const unmount = mount(cache, 'x', () => { calls++; });\n  const first = unmount();\n  expect(unmount()).toBe(first);\n  await first;\n  expect(unmount()).toBe(first);\n  expect(calls).toBe(1);\n});\n\ntest('synchronous failure rejects completion and still invalidates', async () => {\n  const cache = createCache();\n  const failure = new Error('failed');\n  const unmount = mount(cache, 'x', () => { throw failure; });\n  await expect(unmount()).rejects.toBe(failure);\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBeUndefined();\n  await expect(unmount()).rejects.toBe(failure);\n});\n\ntest('async failure cleans only its ownership', async () => {\n  const cache = createCache();\n  const failure = new Error('async failed');\n  const old = mount(cache, 'x', async () => { throw failure; });\n  const value = { ready: 'replacement' };\n  const latest = mount(cache, 'x', () => {}, value);\n  await expect(old()).rejects.toBe(failure);\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBe(value);\n  await latest();\n});\n\ntest('cache instances isolate identical keys', async () => {\n  const a = createCache();\n  const b = createCache();\n  const unmountA = mount(a, 'x', () => {}, { ready: 'a' });\n  const valueB = { ready: 'b' };\n  const unmountB = mount(b, 'x', () => {}, valueB);\n  await unmountA();\n  expect(a.get('x')).toBeUndefined();\n  expect(b.get('x')).toBe(valueB);\n  await unmountB();\n});\n\ntest('async report is awaited and reentrant replacement survives', async () => {\n  const cache = createCache();\n  let release;\n  const gate = new Promise(ok => { release = ok; });\n  const original = { ready: 'original' };\n  let replacement;\n  const unmount = mount(cache, 'x', async () => {\n    await gate;\n    replacement = mount(cache, 'x', () => {}, { ready: 'replacement' });\n  }, original);\n  const done = unmount();\n  await Promise.resolve();\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBe(original);\n  release();\n  await done;\n  expect(cache.get('x').ready).toBe('replacement');\n  await replacement();\n});\n"
    },

      "owner": "local-013-arena-walkthrough-early-repair",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "export function createCache() {\n  const entries = new Map();\n  return {\n    put(key, value) {\n      const owner = Symbol('mount');\n      entries.set(key, { owner, value });\n      return owner;\n    },\n    get(key) { return entries.get(key)?.value; },\n    invalidate(key, owner) {\n      if (entries.get(key)?.owner !== owner) return false;\n      return entries.delete(key);\n    },\n  };\n}\n"

      "text": "# Synthesis evidence\n\nInput revision 5453137ccc4e5d1f0b78726eabd8d13295ba0468. Frozen package 0.1.3, operative source freeze 51f209daf83cd97d64f89881d66533bb59dc57db. A's entry design is valid but changes keys into labels and removes lookup.\n\nGrafted A's single finally cleanup path and value release after settlement into B. These changes keep one ownership model.\n\nRejected A's entry.read/state API because it duplicates the cache/token ownership mechanism. Rejected timers, globals, late key lookup, unconditional deletion and swallowed failures. No candidate dropout occurred. Both metadata correction attempts preserved original bytes separately; implementation bytes were not changed by those corrections.\n\nFresh judge inspected both complete artifacts after their terminal results and confirmed 13 candidate tests, 53 assertions and two successful probes. The parent's synthesis verification ran 10 tests, 29 assertions, with exit 0. Its actual probe printed disposed ready: true and teardown completed, exit 0. git diff --exit-code exited 0 and HEAD remained the exact input revision. Raw parent verification is ../raw/synthesis-verification.json.\n\nVerification covers deferred reads, duplicate keys, replacements, repeat disposal, callback errors, independent cache owners, asynchronous settlement, invalid report input and cleanup failure. Reference clearing was inspected in code; heap reclamation was not measured. Never-settling callbacks retain pending values; self-await deadlocks. No cancellation or timeout policy is implemented. Compatibility claims cover only the pinned local disposer.\n\nThe historical invalidation.diff remains provenance, not the synthesis patch. README.md now describes the current implementation. See ../method-receipt.json, ../judge.md and ../arena-walkthrough.result.md for orchestration evidence and limits.\n\n"

    {
      "path": "reruns/local-01/arena-walkthrough/outputs/synthesis/README.md",
      "bytes": 1266,
      "sha256": "7bbc6ffe28e591fb576c8ec23d9754ef8479bcf62638d9d8d8d4d8b439b144aa",
      "owner": "local-013-arena-walkthrough-early-repair",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "# Local cache synthesis\n\nBase candidate B preserves keyed lookup through createCache(). Each mount captures its exact value. Teardown reports that value, awaits the callback, then conditionally invalidates its ownership token. An older mount cannot remove a same-key replacement. Each cache owns a separate Map.\n\nThe unmount function returns one completion promise. Handle rejection. Captured value and callback references are cleared after cleanup, including failures. External aliases can still retain objects; no garbage-collection measurement is claimed.\n\nRun from the fixture root:\n\n- bun test outputs/synthesis/cache.test.mjs\n- bun outputs/synthesis/probe.mjs\n\nThe vendored microtask disposer is the exact pinned local fixture. No public dependency compatibility is claimed. A callback that never settles keeps its mount pending and retains its value. A report must not await its own unmount promise. Values are mutable references. This design has no cancellation or timeout policy.\n\nThe supplied manifest describes the unchanged vendor bytes. invalidation.diff is a historical input showing the original bug, not the synthesis patch. The untouched baseline remains in outputs/working/cache. See SYNTHESIS.md for the base, grafts, rejections and verification.\n"

    {
      "path": "reruns/local-01/arena-walkthrough/outputs/synthesis/caller.mjs",
      "bytes": 933,
      "sha256": "9b574edfb16be26c0afb6dfd06b700ebc08dc0ee82aae8c32a860aecc9d1cc7c",
      "owner": "local-013-arena-walkthrough-early-repair",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import { createDisposer } from './vendor/disposer-v1.mjs';\nasync function disposeCaptured(value, report) {\n  await report(value.ready);\n}\nexport function mount(cache, key, report, value = { ready: true }) {\n  if (typeof report !== 'function') throw new TypeError('report must be a function');\n  const owner = cache.put(key, value);\n  let completion;\n  let resolve;\n  let reject;\n  const subscription = createDisposer(() => {\n    const finish = async () => {\n      try {\n        await disposeCaptured(value, report);\n      } finally {\n        try {\n          cache.invalidate(key, owner);\n        } finally {\n          value = undefined;\n          report = undefined;\n        }\n      }\n    };\n    finish().then(resolve, reject);\n  });\n  return function unmount() {\n    if (!completion) {\n      completion = new Promise((ok, fail) => { resolve = ok; reject = fail; });\n      subscription.dispose();\n    }\n    return completion;\n  };\n}\n"
    },

      "owner": "local-013-arena-walkthrough-early-repair",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "{\n  \"scope\": \"exact local vendored fixture only\",\n  \"dependency\": {\n    \"path\": \"vendor/disposer-v1.mjs\",\n    \"version\": \"fixture-v1\",\n    \"sha256\": \"d33e8d36600ad5df008657e478e39f9100a347098b4176f37923e5056cb3427f\"\n  },\n  \"publicPackageClaim\": false\n}\n"

    {
      "path": "reruns/local-01/arena-walkthrough/outputs/synthesis/cache.test.mjs",
      "bytes": 4466,
      "sha256": "62c9f3f55ba7ca9d6f2f41167dd1af8f628e58aac8b5259f873d8b80619f1e57",
      "owner": "local-013-arena-walkthrough-early-repair",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import { test, expect } from 'bun:test';\nimport { createCache } from './cache.mjs';\nimport { mount } from './caller.mjs';\n\ntest('successful asynchronous disposal preserves access until settlement', async () => {\n  const cache = createCache();\n  let release;\n  const gate = new Promise(resolve => { release = resolve; });\n  const value = { ready: 'held' };\n  const seen = [];\n  const unmount = mount(cache, 'pending', async ready => {\n    seen.push(ready);\n    expect(cache.get('pending')).toBe(value);\n    await gate;\n    expect(cache.get('pending')).toBe(value);\n  }, value);\n  const done = unmount();\n  await Promise.resolve();\n  expect(cache.get('pending')).toBe(value);\n  release();\n  await done;\n  expect(seen).toEqual(['held']);\n  expect(cache.get('pending')).toBeUndefined();\n});\n\ntest('invalid report leaves the existing cache owner untouched', async () => {\n  const cache = createCache();\n  const value = { ready: 'existing' };\n  const unmount = mount(cache, 'x', () => {}, value);\n  expect(() => mount(cache, 'x', null)).toThrow(TypeError);\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBe(value);\n  await unmount();\n});\n\ntest('cleanup failure rejects the completion rather than leaving it pending', async () => {\n  const failure = new Error('cleanup failed');\n  const cache = { put() { return Symbol('owner'); }, invalidate() { throw failure; } };\n  const unmount = mount(cache, 'x', () => {});\n  await expect(unmount()).rejects.toBe(failure);\n});\n\n\ntest('deferred callback reads mounted value before invalidation', async () => {\n  const cache = createCache();\n  const value = { ready: true };\n  const seen = [];\n  const unmount = mount(cache, 'x', ready => { seen.push(ready); expect(cache.get('x')).toBe(value); }, value);\n  const done = unmount();\n  expect(seen).toEqual([]);\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBe(value);\n  await done;\n  expect(seen).toEqual([true]);\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBeUndefined();\n});\n\ntest('duplicate keys capture distinct values and preserve replacement', async () => {\n  const cache = createCache();\n  const seen = [];\n  const old = mount(cache, 'x', ready => seen.push(ready), { ready: 'old' });\n  const value = { ready: 'new' };\n  const latest = mount(cache, 'x', ready => seen.push(ready), value);\n  await old();\n  expect(seen).toEqual(['old']);\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBe(value);\n  await latest();\n  expect(seen).toEqual(['old', 'new']);\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBeUndefined();\n});\n\ntest('repeat disposal shares completion and reports once', async () => {\n  const cache = createCache();\n  let calls = 0;\n  const unmount = mount(cache, 'x', () => { calls++; });\n  const first = unmount();\n  expect(unmount()).toBe(first);\n  await first;\n  expect(unmount()).toBe(first);\n  expect(calls).toBe(1);\n});\n\ntest('synchronous failure rejects completion and still invalidates', async () => {\n  const cache = createCache();\n  const failure = new Error('failed');\n  const unmount = mount(cache, 'x', () => { throw failure; });\n  await expect(unmount()).rejects.toBe(failure);\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBeUndefined();\n  await expect(unmount()).rejects.toBe(failure);\n});\n\ntest('async failure cleans only its ownership', async () => {\n  const cache = createCache();\n  const failure = new Error('async failed');\n  const old = mount(cache, 'x', async () => { throw failure; });\n  const value = { ready: 'replacement' };\n  const latest = mount(cache, 'x', () => {}, value);\n  await expect(old()).rejects.toBe(failure);\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBe(value);\n  await latest();\n});\n\ntest('cache instances isolate identical keys', async () => {\n  const a = createCache();\n  const b = createCache();\n  const unmountA = mount(a, 'x', () => {}, { ready: 'a' });\n  const valueB = { ready: 'b' };\n  const unmountB = mount(b, 'x', () => {}, valueB);\n  await unmountA();\n  expect(a.get('x')).toBeUndefined();\n  expect(b.get('x')).toBe(valueB);\n  await unmountB();\n});\n\ntest('async report is awaited and reentrant replacement survives', async () => {\n  const cache = createCache();\n  let release;\n  const gate = new Promise(ok => { release = ok; });\n  const original = { ready: 'original' };\n  let replacement;\n  const unmount = mount(cache, 'x', async () => {\n    await gate;\n    replacement = mount(cache, 'x', () => {}, { ready: 'replacement' });\n  }, original);\n  const done = unmount();\n  await Promise.resolve();\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBe(original);\n  release();\n  await done;\n  expect(cache.get('x').ready).toBe('replacement');\n  await replacement();\n});\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "reruns/local-01/arena-walkthrough/outputs/synthesis/cache.mjs",
      "bytes": 386,
      "sha256": "b36aeef88de399d99fdb5b327036ae61ffea148d8ace20f179986bbee252f3ab",
      "owner": "local-013-arena-walkthrough-early-repair",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "export function createCache() {\n  const entries = new Map();\n  return {\n    put(key, value) {\n      const owner = Symbol('mount');\n      entries.set(key, { owner, value });\n      return owner;\n    },\n    get(key) { return entries.get(key)?.value; },\n    invalidate(key, owner) {\n      if (entries.get(key)?.owner !== owner) return false;\n      return entries.delete(key);\n    },\n  };\n}\n"
    },

      "text": "// Exact vendored fixture dependency implementation, pinned by local SHA-256 in manifest.json.\nexport function createDisposer(onDispose) {\n  return { dispose: () => queueMicrotask(onDispose) };\n}\n"

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "// Exact vendored fixture dependency implementation, pinned by local SHA-256 in manifest.json.\nexport function createDisposer(onDispose) {\n  return { dispose: () => queueMicrotask(onDispose) };\n}\n"

    {
      "path": "reruns/local-01/arena-walkthrough/outputs/candidate-a/README.md",
      "bytes": 2701,
      "sha256": "3262eebb84dbf70beccaf470f7f7706d7ca415e36988df1dee6bcf9708e9c787",
      "owner": "local-013-arena-walkthrough-early-repair",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "# Candidate A: lifecycle-owned entry\n\nAssignment: arena-candidate-a. Seat: candidate-a. Method: arena.\nInput revision: 5453137ccc4e5d1f0b78726eabd8d13295ba0468.\nRequested model/effort: inherit-parent. Actual model/effort: unknown.\n\nEach mount creates an isolated entry. Its key is diagnostic metadata, not a global lookup identity. The entry owns its value and progresses from mounted to disposing to disposed. The actual pinned disposer still queues a microtask. The callback reads entry.read() while the entry is disposing; finally clears the value after the callback settles. No module-level mutable state remains.\n\ndispose(callback) returns the same promise on every call, schedules once, and uses only the first callback. read() throws after disposal, including when the original value was undefined. Synchronous exceptions and rejected promises reject disposal after cleanup. Await the returned promise, or handle its rejection. Async callbacks are supported; a callback that never settles retains the value indefinitely. A callback must not await its own disposal promise, which would deadlock. The object does not deep-freeze or clone mounted values.\n\nDuplicate keys intentionally identify independent lifecycles. Disposing an older mount cannot delete or replace a newer mount with the same label. This removes shared key-based retrieval, so callers needing a shared registry must own that registry separately and specify its collision/ownership contract.\n\nRejected alternatives:\n- Timer-delayed deletion depends on scheduling order and still permits one owner to delete another owner's reused key.\n- A global Map with generation tokens fixes stale deletion but preserves shared mutable state and complicates ownership.\n- Passing a captured value directly to disposal is a valid alternative but belongs to candidate-b; this seat reads through a lifecycle-owned entry.\n- Immediate invalidation plus swallowed callback errors loses teardown access and hides failures.\n\nRun from the fixture root:\n- bun outputs/candidate-a/input/probe.mjs: exit 1, reproduced original TypeError.\n- bun test outputs/candidate-a/implementation/cache.test.mjs: exit 0, 6 tests, 32 assertions.\n- bun outputs/candidate-a/implementation/probe.mjs: exit 0, reported disposed ready: true and teardown completed.\n- bun --version: exit 0, 1.4.2.\n\nThe input/ tree is the unchanged supplied fixture; implementation/ is the runnable redesign. vendor/disposer-v1.mjs is unchanged and only the local dependency behavior is claimed. manifest.json and invalidation.diff in implementation/ retain input provenance and describe the old fixture, not a new patch. No dependencies were installed and no external service was accessed.\n"
    },

    {
      "path": "reruns/local-01/arena-walkthrough/outputs/candidate-a/implementation/cache.test.mjs",
      "bytes": 2707,
      "sha256": "4966e32a82121c000db5aee2db5b9f3847dfc9fe149bc952772af4c62bb9ddbf",
      "owner": "local-013-arena-walkthrough-early-repair",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import { test, expect } from 'bun:test';\nimport { createEntry } from './cache.mjs';\nimport { mount } from './caller.mjs';\n\ntest('real caller reads its entry during deferred disposal', async () => {\n  const reports = [];\n  const unmount = mount('same-key', ready => reports.push(ready));\n  const completion = unmount();\n  expect(reports).toEqual([]);\n  expect(unmount()).toBe(completion);\n  await completion;\n  await unmount();\n  expect(reports).toEqual([true]);\n});\n\ntest('duplicate labels cannot replace or invalidate another owner', async () => {\n  const a = createEntry('duplicate', { id: 'a' });\n  const b = createEntry('duplicate', { id: 'b' });\n  const seen = [];\n  const first = a.dispose(() => seen.push(a.read().id));\n  expect(a.state).toBe('disposing');\n  expect(a.read().id).toBe('a');\n  expect(b.read().id).toBe('b');\n  await first;\n  expect(a.state).toBe('disposed');\n  expect(() => a.read()).toThrow('disposed');\n  expect(b.state).toBe('mounted');\n  await b.dispose(() => seen.push(b.read().id));\n  expect(seen).toEqual(['a', 'b']);\n});\n\ntest('entry stays readable through asynchronous teardown', async () => {\n  let release;\n  const gate = new Promise(resolve => { release = resolve; });\n  const entry = createEntry('async', 42);\n  const completion = entry.dispose(async () => {\n    expect(entry.read()).toBe(42);\n    await gate;\n    expect(entry.read()).toBe(42);\n  });\n  await Promise.resolve();\n  expect(entry.state).toBe('disposing');\n  release();\n  await completion;\n  expect(entry.state).toBe('disposed');\n});\n\nfor (const asynchronous of [false, true]) {\n  test('callback failure invalidates and rejects once, async=' + asynchronous, async () => {\n    const entry = createEntry('failure', 17);\n    const failure = new Error('teardown failed');\n    let calls = 0;\n    const callback = () => {\n      calls++;\n      expect(entry.read()).toBe(17);\n      if (asynchronous) return Promise.reject(failure);\n      throw failure;\n    };\n    const completion = entry.dispose(callback);\n    const observed = completion.catch(error => error);\n    expect(entry.dispose(() => { throw new Error('must not run'); })).toBe(completion);\n    expect(await observed).toBe(failure);\n    expect(entry.state).toBe('disposed');\n    expect(() => entry.read()).toThrow();\n    expect(entry.dispose(callback)).toBe(completion);\n    expect(calls).toBe(1);\n  });\n}\n\ntest('invalid callback leaves entry mounted and undefined is a valid value', async () => {\n  const entry = createEntry('validation', undefined);\n  expect(() => entry.dispose(null)).toThrow(TypeError);\n  expect(entry.state).toBe('mounted');\n  expect(entry.read()).toBeUndefined();\n  await entry.dispose(() => expect(entry.read()).toBeUndefined());\n});\n"
