      "text": "{\"arguments\":{\"cmd\":\"cat /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/references/host-capabilities.md /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/references/model-roles.md /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/references/orchestration-contract.md /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/references/workflow-ownership.md\",\"max_output_tokens\":16000},\"return\":{\"chunk_id\":\"e4974e\",\"wall_time_seconds\":0.000005584,\"exit_code\":0,\"original_token_count\":4391,\"output\":\"# Discover capabilities in the current session\\n\\nRead the tools exposed to this session before assigning work. Cached official-subagents.txt is documentation context; it proves no operation succeeded. Local agent configuration is not portable plugin configuration.\\n\\nRecord each binding as `{operation, tool, exposed, succeeded, evidence, limits}`. `tool` is the exact exposed identifier or null when absent. `succeeded` is true only after observing a result. Keep failed and unavailable bindings. Successful bindings become `successfulOperations` in host evidence, with a root-relative evidence file. The operation labels below describe purposes, never callable APIs.\\n\\n| Operation | Discovery and observation required |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| spawn | Find an exposed independent-worker operation; retain returned worker identity and exact assigned revision. |\\n| follow-up | Find the operation that sends input to that worker; observe acceptance by the same identity. |\\n| wait | Find the operation that waits for worker state; retain terminal or interrupted state. |\\n| inspect-result | Read the worker result and its referenced artifacts; a wait notification alone is insufficient. |\\n| stop | Observe cancellation or termination through the exposed operation. |\\n| read | Observe the requested file content through the available file tool. |\\n| isolated-write | Observe a write within the worker's assigned path and permissions. |\\n| history | Observe available prior turns or records; declare gaps explicitly. |\\n| execution | Observe command execution with exit status and output. |\\n| persistence | Write and read an authorized durable record; a claimed save is insufficient. |\\n| external-write | Record explicit authorization and action identity; inspect the result before replay. |\\n| resolve-ownership | Observe distinct owned paths before contested writes. |\\n| inspect-terminal | Observe the worker's terminal state after stop. |\\n| quarantine-artifacts | Observe partial artifacts withheld from integration. |\\n| inspect-prior-action | Read the interrupted action identity and prior outcome. |\\n| inspect-destination | Observe the destination state for that action identity. |\\n| safe-recovery | Observe explicitly authorized idempotent recovery after identity and destination inspection. |\\n\\nNo default API names are assigned here. Tool names differ by host and session. An exposed tool may still be denied or fail. Record requested and actual models only when observed; otherwise use `unknown`. A requested model never proves the actual model.\\n\\nA denied or unavailable operation blocks the branch that requires it. Sequential substitution for required independent work is reduced capability and uses `reduced-pass`; ordinary direct completion can fully pass. Missing persistence limits session pickup even when current work succeeds. Preserve user authorization and host permission boundaries through every fallback.\\n\\nWorker passes require observed spawn and result inspection. Each registry entry declares `requiredObservations` for `pass` and `reduced-pass`; tool observations need exposed bindings and existing evidence artifacts; native text observations use the separate reviewed native record below. Full cancellation requires stop, terminal inspection and artifact quarantine. Full persistence requires durable write and readback. Full interrupted-action recovery requires prior identity inspection, destination inspection, safe recovery, explicit external permission and a recorded prior action identity even when no external-write observation is listed.\\n\\nPermission checks follow performed operations. Isolated writes and persistence require granted writes. External writes and safe recovery require granted external permission and prior identity. Authorized read-only reductions may retain denied writes; their limits must preserve denied or unavailable permissions. Required observations remain applicable to those reductions.\\n\\nHost evidence is stored as object or array JSON files under `docs/parity/evidence/`. Required fields are defined by `docs/parity/evidence.schema.json`. Artifacts and operation evidence must be existing files inside the tested root. Test fixtures belong in `tests/` and prove validator behavior only.\\n\\nRun `python3 tools/validate_evidence.py --root . --commit <tested-package-commit>` through Bun, for example `bun -e 'const p=Bun.spawnSync([\\\"python3\\\",\\\"-B\\\",\\\"tools/validate_evidence.py\\\",\\\"--root\\\",\\\".\\\",\\\"--commit\\\",process.argv[1]],{env:{...process.env,PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE:\\\"1\\\"}});process.stdout.write(p.stdout);process.stderr.write(p.stderr);process.exit(p.exitCode)' <tested-package-commit>`. It reads every JSON record below the evidence directory, prints each error, and exits 1 for invalid records or 0 for valid records. An empty directory has no invalid records and supplies no behavioral evidence.\\n\\nThe required registry file in `docs/parity/case-registry.json` declares applicability. Missing or non-file registry, unknown case, structural-only entry or unlisted host rejects behavioral validation. Maintenance fixtures use a temporary copy of this registry; they cannot bypass applicability. Required hosts must receive observed evidence or explicit blocked records before release claims. Structural checks have no required host and cannot populate host status. Later producers propose task-owned entries; only the coordinator integrates them. Source paths select callers through the task 3 case contract. Case definitions alone leave host statuses `not-run`.\\n\\n## Direct completion and recorded observations\\n\\n`direct` means the task is completed in the current context. Restatement, supplied-text writing and complete installed discovery can pass directly. `sequential` is reserved for replacing a required independent method with sequential work and remains reduced. A text response has no invented callable tool. Record supplied input, the actual response and qualitative outcome review as `nativeObservations`, each with its existing listed evidence artifact and named reviewer. Their labels are `supplied-input`, `response` and `review-outcome`. The reviewer assesses the case's expected outcome; validation checks evidence relationships and does not decide prose quality.\\n\\nEach registry entry declares allowed execution modes and required permissions for each status. A grant is required for the performed action: worker spawn, command execution and stop need execution; isolated output or persistence needs writes; external actions need their separate permission and prior identity. Read-only discovery does not inherit an execution grant requirement. Tool observations still name an actually exposed tool and existing evidence. Native observations cannot claim tool discovery, worker identity or saved writes.\\n\\nFull Arena and Swarm results additionally provide `inputRevision` and a listed `methodReceipt` artifact. An exposed `inspect-method` operation must reference that receipt. Assignment operations name `assignmentId` and the corresponding inspected output. See the [structured method contract](orchestration-contract.md). All positive maintenance fixtures are synthetic; none is an observed host result.\\n# Model selection for portable roles\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](host-capabilities.md) before assigning a role. These [poteto](agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md) and [comment reviewer](agent-prompts/comment-sicko.md) prompts are instructions supplied to an exposed worker operation. Reading them does not register a custom agent or authorize delegation.\\n\\n| Role | Default requested model | Observed model | Supported effort | Fallback disclosure |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| poteto-agent | inherit-parent | unknown until observed | inherit-parent unless a supported explicit effort is verified | Record rejected selection, replacement request, observed result and limits. |\\n| comment-sicko | inherit-parent | unknown until observed | inherit-parent unless a supported explicit effort is verified | Record rejected selection, replacement request, observed result and limits. |\\n\\nFor each assignment, record requested model and effort, observed model and effort, supported effort values and their source, worker identity, and fallback disclosure. Use `unknown` for information the operation does not expose. `inherit-parent` records a selection policy, not an observed model name. Do not silently convert a requested model into an actual model.\\n\\nSelect an explicit model only from current exposed tool documentation or observed enumeration results. If enumeration is missing, disclose that limit and retain `inherit-parent`. Documentation examples are not a list of available models. Use only an effort supported for the selected model by the current operation; do not carry an incompatible inherited effort into an explicit selection.\\n\\nIf a selected model or effort is rejected, retain the rejection. Use an authorized inherited or supported alternative only after disclosing the changed selection. If the task requires that exact selection, stop and record blocked. A fallback never proves the original selection succeeded.\\n\\nIdentical observed models mean no model diversity. Different roles can supply distinct instructions on the same model. Unknown observed models leave diversity unverified, even when requested model names differ. Different observed models support a model-diversity statement only for those observed assignments. Worker independence still requires successful spawn and result inspection.\\n\\nWhen workers are unavailable, apply an authorized role sequentially and label reduced capability. Preserve scope and permission boundaries. Do not claim independent review, background execution, or full worker support from sequential role switching.\\n\\nThe cached documentation from https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents describes inheritance and optional local agent configuration. It is context only. This package writes no local custom-agent configuration and claims no current host model or worker support from that documentation.\\n# Assignment and integration contract\\n\\nBefore dispatch, the coordinator creates an immutable assignment with `id`, `scope`, `inputRevision`, `outputOwner`, `isolatedOutputPath`, `role`, `retryCount`, `terminalStatus`, and `evidenceLinks`. Use the full Git SHA for inputRevision, an exact owned path, and an explicit role. Start retryCount at 0 and terminalStatus at `pending`. Preserve every attempt as an append-only event under the same assignment ID; update status through events, never rewrite the original scope, revision, owner or path. A changed scope or revision requires a new assignment ID that links its predecessor.\\n\\nThe coordinator checks authorization and observed host bindings before dispatch. One path has one writer. Reject overlapping paths before work starts; assign distinct paths instead. Workers write only their isolated output and report results. Only the coordinator integrates shared files, inventory, registry, or other workers' output.\\n\\nAccept a result only when its assignment identity and input SHA match, its artifacts exist, and required method evidence was observed. Reject stale revisions. Permit at most one retry for missing required SHA or method evidence, after inspecting the prior attempt and confirming the same permissions still apply. A retry count of 1 exhausts this allowance. Denied permissions, unknown action outcomes, and missing artifacts never become success by retry policy.\\n\\nTerminal states are `completed`, `blocked`, `failed`, and `cancelled`. A completion event links the exact result and evidence. Stop a cancelled worker through the exposed stop binding when available, then inspect its terminal state. Quarantine any partial artifacts; cancellation does not authorize their integration. If stop cannot be observed, record that limit and do not claim termination. Report interrupted execution explicitly.\\n\\nBefore an external action, record explicit permission, a stable action identity, the intended destination and the last observed outcome. After interruption, inspect whether that identity already completed. Retry only with authorization, an observed safe replay decision and an idempotency mechanism appropriate to the destination. If the outcome is unknown, block replay. Do not infer permission from upstream autonomy instructions.\\n\\nHistory and persistence have separate bindings. Keep assignment events and result links in an authorized durable location and verify readback. If unavailable, declare the gap and offer an authorized local handoff as reduced capability; never claim unattended recovery or cross-session continuity. All host statuses remain `not-run` until actual observations exist.\\n\\n## Structured Arena and Swarm receipts\\n\\nA method receipt is JSON with schemaVersion 1, kind `arena` or `swarm`, inputRevision, assignments, reviewArtifact, reviewedBy and declaredOrder. The inputRevision is the actual task repository revision, distinct from the packageCommit identifying these instructions. It must match the evidence record. The declared order precedes every dispatch. reviewArtifact records the qualitative outcome review and reviewedBy identifies its reviewer. All referenced artifacts must exist and be listed in the evidence record.\\n\\nEach assignment records id, workerId, inputRevision, outputOwner, outputPath, role, status, startedOrder, completedOrder, requestedModel, actualModel, retryCount, method, taskArtifact, rubricProvided, resultRevision, resultMethod and outputSha256. Result revision and method must match the assignment, and the inspected output bytes must match their digest. Worker and assignment identities are distinct. outputOwner equals workerId; output directories do not overlap. Integer order values record the observed dispatch and completion sequence, not estimated time. The method has positive sampleCount, sampleDefinition and order. Missing model observations use unknown. The validator requires assignment-bound spawn and result inspection, and isolated-write for output-producing candidates. A read-only judge may return its result through the coordinator's authorized artifact capture. A cancelled result needs bound stop, terminal inspection and quarantine observations. No operation string alone establishes a method.\\n\\nArena adds candidates, judge, rubricArtifact and synthesis. At least two candidates share the same taskArtifact, finish before a distinct fresh judge starts and do not receive the parent rubric. Synthesis has order, inspectedCandidates, artifact and verificationArtifact; it follows completed judgment and accounts for every candidate. The review artifact assesses scoring, base selection, grafts, rejections and verification quality. File presence and phase ordering do not establish the quality of those decisions.\\n\\nSwarm adds partition, race, cancelled and quarantined. Partition declares requiredSlices, results mapping each slice to its assignment, and gaps. A full coverage claim requires all slices with completed inspected outputs; gaps remain explicit reduced or blocked work. Race declares rule, assignments, winner and ruleArtifact. first-pass must select the first completed survivor; rank-all needs all results; best-of retains an explicit reviewed selection. Cancelled assignments must be quarantined and cannot enter the aggregate. The combined partition-and-race case requires both methods and its cancellation exercise. The partition walkthrough exercises only its declared slices; it does not acquire an unrelated race requirement.\\n\\nThe three-file Swarm walkthrough requires exactly three declared slices and three completed results. Its partition-only receipt uses race null and empty cancellation, quarantine and failureExercises arrays. The combined case also records failureExercises. Each event has assignmentId, kind, attempt, order, reason and evidence, with bound result-rejection or terminal inspection. Rejected missing-revision or missing-method evidence uses attempts 0 then 1; a second invalid result exhausts the retry and leaves a failed or blocked assignment. A separate failed or blocked dropout is disclosed. These failed outputs cannot satisfy required coverage. The final assignment result metadata records the inspected terminal summary; rejection-event artifacts retain the invalid attempts.\\n# Workflow ownership\\n\\nAn explicit pstack invocation gives pstack ownership of that workflow. An explicit Superpowers invocation gives Superpowers ownership. Do not run both controllers over the same assignment or let one silently replace the other's plan, review, or integration decisions.\\n\\nFor an unqualified request, D1 retains the already active workflow. With no active workflow, use host defaults and do not activate either orchestration mode automatically. If both pstack and Superpowers are explicitly requested, clarify ownership before launching workers or changing artifacts. Preserve the active controller across follow-ups unless the user changes ownership. A helper skill can advise the owner without becoming a second controller.\\n\\nThe owner assigns one coordinator. Workers produce isolated artifacts and evidence; the coordinator reviews and integrates them. Shared inventory and registry writes belong to the coordinator. Worker cancellation, stale results or unavailable tools do not transfer that ownership automatically.\\n\\nHost permissions and user authorization constrain every owner. Local structural tests, documented APIs and declared cases provide no host pass. Explicit reduced or blocked results remain visible beside the full expectation.\\n\"}}\n"

});\\n  const value = { ready: 'replacement' };\\n  const latest = mount(cache, 'x', () => {}, value);\\n  await expect(old()).rejects.toBe(failure);\\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBe(value);\\n  await latest();\\n});\\n\\ntest('cache instances isolate identical keys', async () => {\\n  const a = createCache();\\n  const b = createCache();\\n  const unmountA = mount(a, 'x', () => {}, { ready: 'a' });\\n  const valueB = { ready: 'b' };\\n  const unmountB = mount(b, 'x', () => {}, valueB);\\n  await unmountA();\\n  expect(a.get('x')).toBeUndefined();\\n  expect(b.get('x')).toBe(valueB);\\n  await unmountB();\\n});\\n\\ntest('async report is awaited and reentrant replacement survives', async () => {\\n  const cache = createCache();\\n  let release;\\n  const gate = new Promise(ok => { release = ok; });\\n  const original = { ready: 'original' };\\n  let replacement;\\n  const unmount = mount(cache, 'x', async () => {\\n    await gate;\\n    replacement = mount(cache, 'x', () => {}, { ready: 'replacement' });\\n  }, original);\\n  const done = unmount();\\n  await Promise.resolve();\\n  expect(cache.get('x')).toBe(original);\\n  release();\\n  await done;\\n  expect(cache.get('x').ready).toBe('replacement');\\n  await replacement();\\n});\\n// Exact vendored fixture dependency implementation, pinned by local SHA-256 in manifest.json.\\nexport function createDisposer(onDispose) {\\n  return { dispose: () => queueMicrotask(onDispose) };\\n}\\n\"}}\n"

      "text": "{\"arguments\":{\"cmd\":\"cat /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/principle-type-system-discipline/SKILL.md /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/principle-boundary-discipline/SKILL.md /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/typescript-best-practices/references/patterns.md\",\"max_output_tokens\":12000},\"return\":{\"chunk_id\":\"3f9b34\",\"wall_time_seconds\":0.000006375,\"exit_code\":0,\"original_token_count\":4336,\"output\":\"---\\nname: principle-type-system-discipline\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when designing types, reviewing a function signature, or writing code in any statically-typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand semantic primitives, parse external data at boundaries, refuse to lie to the compiler, exhaust variants, derive from authoritative schemas.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Type System Discipline\\n\\nThe type checker is a proof assistant. Use it to eliminate impossible states, mismatched primitives, and unhandled variants at compile time. A case the types let you ignore becomes a runtime failure the compiler could have stopped. Prefer defining errors and special cases out of existence over proliferating handlers. Unrepresentable states, total functions, and interface redesign (the patterns below) are the tools.\\n\\nApplies to any typed language. Skills like `typescript-best-practices` ground it in specific syntax.\\n\\n**The patterns:**\\n\\n- **Make illegal states unrepresentable.** Model variants as sum types: discriminated unions in TypeScript, enums with payloads in Rust/Swift/Kotlin, sealed classes in Scala, ADTs in Haskell/OCaml. Don't model state as a bag of optional fields where contradictory combinations compile. A subtle anti-pattern: `{ completed: boolean; completedAt?: Date }` admits `completed: true; completedAt: undefined`, which is meaningless. Derive the boolean from a single source like `completedAt !== null`, or model the variants explicitly as `{ kind: 'open' } | { kind: 'done'; at: Date }`. If a bug forces the question \\\"wait, can this combination actually happen?\\\", the type is too loose.\\n- **Types are constructions, not restrictions.** Build the type up from the values you want instead of carving them out of a looser type with checks. The invariant that seems to need a refinement type is usually a construction away. A non-empty list is a head plus a rest, not a list with a length check. A valid time range is a start plus a duration, not two timestamps you must keep ordered. No representation is privileged. A list of pairs is an even-length list if you interpret it that way, so choose the shape that cannot build the illegal value and expose the interface callers need on top.\\n- **Brand semantic primitives.** `UserId` and `OrderId` are strings underneath but should not be interchangeable. Newtypes in Rust, opaque types in Swift, value classes in Kotlin, phantom types in Haskell, branded intersections in TypeScript. Validate once at creation, trust the type downstream.\\n- **External data is untyped until parsed.** RPC payloads, JSON, IPC messages, CLI args, config files, environment variables, database rows. Have a parse function at every boundary that turns unstructured input into the typed model. See the **boundary-discipline** principle skill for where to put validation.\\n- **Don't lie to the type system.** Casts, unsafe coercions, and assertion functions that bypass the compiler are latent runtime crashes. If the compiler can't prove a fact, prove it (validate, narrow, refine the model) or accept that the cast is a hazard.\\n- **Exhaustive matching is the compiler's job.** When you match on a sum type, the compiler must fail compilation if a new variant is added without handling. Use the idiom your language provides: `never`-typed binding in TypeScript, unannotated `match` in Rust, `-Wincomplete-patterns` in Haskell, sealed-class match exhaustiveness in Kotlin.\\n- **Derive types from authoritative schemas.** When a protocol buffer, OpenAPI spec, GraphQL schema, database migration, or design-system token file defines a shape, derive from it instead of hand-rolling a parallel type. See the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill.\\n- **Strengthen a type only where partiality appears.** A runtime assertion, null check, or \\\"this should never happen\\\" throw marks the place a type is too weak. Push that check up into the type. Then stop. The type system's job is to track the cases each use site must handle, not to describe the data as precisely as possible. Prefer total functions. `sum` of an empty list is 0, so it takes the plain list. `head` of an empty list has no answer, so it demands the non-empty one.\\n\\n**The tests:**\\n\\n- \\\"Can I write a comment explaining when this combination of fields is valid?\\\" If yes, the type is too loose. Split it into a sum type.\\n- \\\"Do two of my function arguments share a primitive type but mean different things?\\\" Brand them.\\n- \\\"Where did this `any`, this `as`, this `assertNotNull` come from?\\\" Trace it to the boundary and validate there instead.\\n- \\\"If a new variant is added next month, will the compiler tell the next agent where to add a case?\\\" If no, the match isn't exhaustive.\\n- \\\"Is this type duplicating a shape another file owns?\\\" Derive instead.\\n- \\\"Am I strengthening this type to keep an operation total, or just to be more precise?\\\" If nothing would otherwise panic, keep the plain type.\\n\\n## Session capabilities and limits\\n\\nFollow [host capability discovery](../../references/host-capabilities.md) for source reads, authorized edits and compiler execution. The metadata above preserves the source invocation policy; do not assume the host enforces it.\\n\\nApply these patterns within the authorized task and exposed tools. If source access, writes or compiler execution are unavailable, provide a reduced proposal and state the missing checks. Identify the actual language limit when an invariant cannot be expressed in its types, and keep the required runtime validation explicit. Do not claim a compiler check ran without observed execution. Missing tools do not authorize installation or external actions.\\n---\\nname: principle-boundary-discipline\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Boundary Discipline\\n\\nPlace validation, type narrowing, and error handling at system boundaries. Trust internal code unconditionally. Business logic lives in pure functions. The shell is thin and mechanical.\\n\\n**Why:** Scattered validation is noisy, redundant, and gives a false sense of safety. Keep logic out of framework wiring so it can be tested without the framework.\\n\\n**The pattern:**\\n- **At boundaries** (CLI args, config files, external APIs, network protocols): validate, return errors, handle defensively.\\n- **Inside the system:** typed data, error propagation, no re-validation. Trust the types.\\n- **Across the boundary.** Expose domain concepts, not the boundary's private representation. Keep general-purpose mechanism inside and special-purpose policy at the edge.\\n\\n**Applications:**\\n\\nValidation and error handling:\\n- Validate config at parse time (the boundary), not inside business logic\\n- Parse raw data into domain types at the boundary\\n- Do not re-export transport, storage, framework, or wire types through the public surface\\n- No redundant nil checks deep in call chains if the boundary already validated\\n\\nCode organization:\\n- Business logic in pure functions with no framework dependencies\\n- Parse functions: pure transforms from raw bytes to typed state\\n- Prompt construction: structured state in, string out\\n- Scoring and assessment: pure transforms from state to results\\n\\n**The tests:**\\n- \\\"Is this data crossing a system boundary right now?\\\" If not, validation is redundant.\\n- \\\"Can this be a pure function that the shell just calls?\\\" If yes, extract it.\\n\\n## Session capabilities and permissions\\n\\nUse [the capability contract](../../references/host-capabilities.md) to check available source access, writes and execution. Preserve user authorization and host permissions. If writes or execution are unavailable, provide a reduced proposal and state which edits or checks were not performed. If required source or input contracts are missing, identify the missing inputs and keep the proposal provisional. Claim implementation and verification only from observed results.\\n\\nPreserve the explicit-invocation metadata above without assuming the host enforces it.\\n# TypeScript patterns\\n\\nCode examples for each rule in `SKILL.md`. The underlying principles are language-agnostic. See the **type-system-discipline** and **boundary-discipline** principle skills.\\n\\n## Branded types\\n\\nBrand primitives so they can't be mixed up. Validate once at the boundary. Downstream code trusts the type.\\n\\n```ts\\ntype AgentId = string & { readonly __brand: \\\"AgentId\\\" };\\n\\nfunction parseAgentId(input: string): AgentId {\\n  if (!isUUID(input)) throw new Error(`Invalid agent id: ${input}`);\\n  return input as AgentId;\\n}\\n\\nfunction focusAgent(id: AgentId): void {\\n  /* input is trusted */\\n}\\n```\\n\\nMatch the `readonly __brand: 'X'` shape. Don't invent a new convention.\\n\\n## Discriminated unions\\n\\nModel variants with a literal discriminant. Every variant shares the field name and each variant's value is unique, so impossible combos can't be represented.\\n\\n```ts\\n// Don't. Boolean + optionals lets contradictory states exist.\\ntype DiffState = { loading: boolean; diff?: GitDiff; error?: string };\\n\\n// Do. Only valid states exist.\\ntype DiffState =\\n  | { kind: \\\"loading\\\" }\\n  | { kind: \\\"ready\\\"; diff: GitDiff }\\n  | { kind: \\\"error\\\"; error: string };\\n```\\n\\nPick one discriminant name (`kind`, `type`, `tag`) and stick to it.\\n\\n## Constructive modeling\\n\\nBuild the type from parts that are all legal instead of restricting a loose type with runtime checks.\\n\\nNon-empty, via a variadic tuple:\\n\\n```ts\\ntype NonEmpty<T> = [T, ...T[]];\\n\\n// Don't: T[] plus a length check every caller must repeat\\nfunction pickWinner(entries: string[]): string {\\n  if (entries.length === 0) throw new Error(\\\"no entries\\\");\\n  return entries[Math.floor(Math.random() * entries.length)];\\n}\\n\\n// Do: an empty value of the type can't exist\\nfunction pickWinner(entries: NonEmpty<string>): string {\\n  return entries[Math.floor(Math.random() * entries.length)];\\n}\\n```\\n\\nWhere a plain `T[]` arrives, narrow once with a guard. The fact then travels in the type:\\n\\n```ts\\nconst isNonEmpty = <T>(arr: T[]): arr is NonEmpty<T> => arr.length > 0;\\n```\\n\\nEven length, as pairs:\\n\\n```ts\\ntype Pairs<T> = [T, T][];\\n```\\n\\nA time range, as start plus duration:\\n\\n```ts\\n// Don't: a comment holds the invariant\\ntype TimeRange = { start: Date; end: Date }; // start <= end\\n\\n// Do: a negative range can't be written; derive end when needed\\ntype TimeRange = { start: Date; durationMs: number };\\n```\\n\\nKeep `durationMs` a plain number. Brand it (per Branded types) only if a raw number could be passed where a duration is expected, not by reflex. Pick the representation that makes the bad state unconstructable, then expose the reading you need on top (`pairs.flat()`, a `rangeEnd()` helper).\\n\\n## Simplest total type\\n\\nDon't strengthen everything. Keep `T[]` when every operation on it is total:\\n\\n```ts\\nconst sum = (xs: number[]) => xs.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0); // [] is 0, fine\\n```\\n\\nStrengthen when the loose type forces a lie at a use site. The tells are `!`, `arr[0] as T`, and a \\\"should never happen\\\" throw:\\n\\n```ts\\n// Don't: partiality smuggled past the compiler\\nfunction newestSession(sessions: Session[]): Session {\\n  return sessions.at(0)!;\\n}\\n\\n// Do: strengthen the input; the assertion disappears\\nfunction newestSession(sessions: NonEmpty<Session>): Session {\\n  return sessions[0];\\n}\\n```\\n\\nWeakening the result to `Session | undefined` is the other total signature.\\n\\n## `unknown` over `any`\\n\\nExternal data is always `unknown`. Narrow before use.\\n\\n```ts\\n// Don't\\nfunction handle(input: any) {\\n  return input.foo.bar;\\n}\\n\\n// Do\\nfunction handle(input: unknown) {\\n  if (typeof input === \\\"object\\\" && input !== null && \\\"foo\\\" in input) {\\n    // narrowed; compiler verifies access\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nExternal sources include RPC payloads, `JSON.parse`, `postMessage`, IPC, file contents, environment variables, database results.\\n\\n## Schemas before hand-rolled guards\\n\\nBefore writing a property-by-property type guard for external data, look for the repository's runtime schema library and existing schemas. Let one schema own validation and derive the TypeScript type from it. Do not maintain a schema, a duplicate interface, and a guard that can drift apart.\\n\\n```ts\\nimport { z } from \\\"zod\\\";\\n\\nconst UserSchema = z.object({\\n  id: z.string().uuid(),\\n  role: z.enum([\\\"admin\\\", \\\"member\\\"]),\\n});\\n\\ntype User = z.infer<typeof UserSchema>;\\n\\nfunction parseUser(input: unknown): User {\\n  return UserSchema.parse(input);\\n}\\n```\\n\\nUse `safeParse` when failure is an expected branch. Use the equivalent inference helper when the repository uses another schema library. Do not add a new schema dependency for one guard. This rule prefers the schema system the codebase already trusts.\\n\\n## No `as` casts\\n\\nEvery `as` is a potential runtime crash. Cast only after the type system has verified the claim.\\n\\n```ts\\nimport { z } from \\\"zod\\\";\\n\\n// Don't\\nconst user = data as User;\\n\\n// Don't\\nfunction isUser(data: unknown): data is User {\\n  return typeof data === \\\"object\\\" && data !== null && \\\"id\\\" in data;\\n}\\n\\n// Do\\nconst userSchema = z.object({ id: z.string(), name: z.string() });\\ntype User = z.infer<typeof userSchema>;\\n\\nfunction parseUser(data: unknown): User {\\n  return userSchema.parse(data);\\n}\\n```\\n\\nWhen the type comes first, annotate the validator with the type it proves. The compiler then rejects a validator that proves less than the type. Remove `name` from the object below and the assignment fails to compile.\\n\\n```ts\\ntype User = { id: string; name: string };\\n\\nconst userSchema: z.ZodType<User> = z.object({ id: z.string(), name: z.string() });\\n```\\n\\nWhen refactoring an `as` out of existing code, identify why TypeScript can't infer:\\n\\n- Missing discriminant: add one, switch to a discriminated union.\\n- Overly wide source type (e.g. `Record<string, unknown>`): narrow it.\\n- Untyped boundary: parse with the schema that owns the shape. Add a schema only where none exists.\\n- Genuinely inexpressible: use a branded type or `satisfies`.\\n\\n## Narrowing hierarchy\\n\\nFrom best to last-resort:\\n\\n1. **Discriminated union switch / if.** Compiler narrows automatically.\\n2. **`in` operator.** `\\\"key\\\" in obj` narrows to variants containing that key.\\n3. **`typeof` / `instanceof`.** For primitives and class instances.\\n4. **User-defined type guard.** When the above aren't enough.\\n5. **`as` cast.** Only after validation.\\n\\n```ts\\nfunction area(s: Shape): number {\\n  if (\\\"radius\\\" in s) return Math.PI * s.radius ** 2; // narrowed to circle\\n  return s.width * s.height; // narrowed to rect\\n}\\n```\\n\\n## Type guards\\n\\nA guard must actually verify the claim. A lying guard is worse than `as`.\\n\\n```ts\\nfunction isCircle(s: Shape): s is Shape & { kind: \\\"circle\\\" } {\\n  return s.kind === \\\"circle\\\";\\n}\\n```\\n\\nPrefer discriminant narrowing when possible.\\n\\n## Exhaustiveness\\n\\nIn default arms, assign the discriminant to a `never`-typed local.\\n\\n```ts\\n// Value-returning switch\\nfunction area(s: Shape): number {\\n  switch (s.kind) {\\n    case \\\"circle\\\":\\n      return Math.PI * s.radius ** 2;\\n    case \\\"rect\\\":\\n      return s.width * s.height;\\n    default: {\\n      const _exhaustive: never = s;\\n      return _exhaustive;\\n    }\\n  }\\n}\\n\\n// Void switch\\nfunction handle(s: Shape): void {\\n  switch (s.kind) {\\n    case \\\"circle\\\":\\n      drawCircle(s);\\n      break;\\n    case \\\"rect\\\":\\n      drawRect(s);\\n      break;\\n    default: {\\n      const _exhaustive: never = s;\\n      void _exhaustive;\\n    }\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nReturn-style in value-returning switches, void-style in statement switches.\\n\\n## `satisfies` over `as`\\n\\n`satisfies` validates without widening literal types.\\n\\n```ts\\n// Don't. Widens, loses literal types.\\nconst config = { theme: \\\"dark\\\", cols: 3 } as Config;\\n\\n// Do. Validates AND preserves literal types.\\nconst config = { theme: \\\"dark\\\", cols: 3 } satisfies Config;\\n// config.theme is \\\"dark\\\" (literal), not string\\n```\\n\\n## Boundary validation\\n\\nValidate once where data crosses in. Trust types inside. See the **boundary-discipline** principle skill.\\n\\n- **Wire formats** (proto, JSON-RPC): parse with `ignoreUnknownFields` so forward-compatible changes don't break old clients.\\n- **Persisted JSON:** versioned blob with a try/catch around the parse.\\n- **Don't re-validate** deep in call chains.\\n\\n## Schema-derived types\\n\\nWhen a `.proto`, OpenAPI spec, GraphQL schema, or database migration already defines a shape, derive from the generated types instead of duplicating them.\\n\\n```ts\\n// Don't. Duplicate shape, drifts when the schema changes.\\ntype CheckSummary = {\\n  totalCount: number;\\n  checks: { name: string; status: string }[];\\n};\\nfunction renderChecks(s: CheckSummary) {\\n  /* ... */\\n}\\n\\n// Do. Derive from the generated schema type.\\nimport type { ChecksMessage } from \\\"<generated module>\\\";\\nfunction renderChecks(s: Pick<ChecksMessage, \\\"totalCount\\\" | \\\"checks\\\">) {\\n  /* ... */\\n}\\n```\\n\\nReach for `Pick`, `Omit`, `Parameters`, `ReturnType`, `Awaited`, `typeof` before writing a new interface.\\n\\n## Object args\\n\\n```ts\\n// Don't. Swap two args, still compiles.\\nopenFile(uri, {\\n  startLineNumber: 10,\\n  startColumn: 1,\\n  endLineNumber: 10,\\n  endColumn: 1,\\n});\\n\\n// Do. Order-independent, self-documenting.\\nopenFile({\\n  uri,\\n  selection: {\\n    startLineNumber: 10,\\n    startColumn: 1,\\n    endLineNumber: 10,\\n    endColumn: 1,\\n  },\\n});\\n```\\n\\nSkip on hot paths: per-frame render, tokenizers, parsers, anything in a tight loop where the allocation cost matters.\\n\"}}\n"

If not, eliminate the sharing. When sharing is real, enforce serialization structurally: lockfiles, sequential phases, exclusive ownership. Instructions and conventions are not concurrency control.\\n\\n**Why:** Concurrent writes to shared state create race conditions that are intermittent, hard to reproduce, and expensive to debug.\\n\\n**Pattern:**\\n1. **Identify shared mutable state** (files both read and write, branches both push to, APIs both define and consume).\\n2. **Default: eliminate the shared write target.** Ask: do these actors need one canonical object, or are they publishing independent facts? A rich interface that hides substantial work is not a deep call chain. If answering a question requires tracing through more than 3 files or layers, flatten it.\\n- **Consolidate decisions.** Do not repeat the same choice in several places. Put it behind one source of truth and pass the result as a simple flag.\\n- **Minimize the diff.** Make the smallest change that solves the problem. A removed rule leaves a gap.\\n\\n### Content\\n\\n3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** \\\"highlighting...\\\", \\\"ensuring...\\\", \\\"reflecting...\\\", \\\"showcasing...\\\", \\\"fostering...\\\". Replace with plain words.\\n8. **Fancy ways to say \\\"is\\\".** \\\"serves as\\\", \\\"stands as\\\", \\\"boasts\\\", \\\"features\\\". Just say \\\"is\\\" or \\\"has\\\".\\n9. **\\\"Not just X, but Y.\\\"** State the point directly instead.\\n10. **Rule of three.** Forcing ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.\\n11. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.\\n12. **False ranges.** \\\"from X to Y\\\" where X and Y aren't on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.\\n\\n### Style\\n\\n13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.\\n14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example. Not as mid-sentence connectors. \\\"If you're coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions\\\" adds nothing with the colon. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. \\\"Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English.\\\" Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.\\n15. **Boldface overuse.** Don't bold every proper noun or acronym.\\n16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: \\\"**Performance:** Performance improved...\\\". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail (\\\"**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.\\\") is fine, not a tell.\\n17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.\\n18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.\\n19. **Curly quotes.** Replace with straight quotes.\\n\\n### Communication artifacts\\n\\n20. **Chatbot phrases.** \\\"I hope this helps!\\\", \\\"Let me know if...\\\", \\\"Of course!\\\", \\\"Certainly!\\\", \\\"Found the smoking gun!\\\" Remove.\\n22. **Sycophantic tone.** \\\"Great question! You're absolutely right!\\\" Respond directly.\\n\\n### Filler\\n\\n23. **Filler phrases.** \\\"In order to\\\" becomes \\\"To\\\". \\\"Due to the fact that\\\" becomes \\\"Because\\\". \\\"It is important to note that\\\" gets deleted.\\n24. **Excessive hedging.** \\\"could potentially possibly be argued that it might\\\" becomes \\\"may\\\".\\n25. **Generic conclusions.** \\\"The future looks bright.\\\" State specific plans or facts.\\n\\n### Jargon\\n\\n26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate, wedge, vector, locus, vantage, nexus, primitive (as noun), harness (as metaphor), surface (as in \\\"API surface\\\"), bedrock, scaffolding (as metaphor), modality, paradigm, gold-plating, ratchet (as metaphor), evacuate (for moving code), endgame, north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. \\\"Substrate\\\" becomes \\\"base\\\". \\\"Wedge in\\\" becomes \\\"add\\\". \\\"Vector\\\" becomes \\\"way\\\" or \\\"method\\\". \\\"Gold-plating\\\" becomes \\\"more than the job needs\\\". \\\"Ratchet\\\" becomes the mechanism's real name or \\\"a limit that only tightens\\\". \\\"Evacuate\\\" becomes \\\"move out\\\". \\\"Endgame\\\" becomes \\\"the last phase\\\". Pick the concrete word.\\n\\n### Plain speech\\n\\n27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** \\\"the database stays close at hand\\\", \\\"SQL you can read\\\", \\\"types that follow your schema\\\" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: \\\"`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database\\\", \\\"a column rename fails the build\\\". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can't restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project's docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.\\n28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.\\n29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. Catch \\\"is/are/was/were + past participle\\\" and name the actor: \\\"queries are validated\\\" becomes \\\"the compiler validates queries\\\", \\\"the file is parsed by the loader\\\" becomes \\\"the loader parses the file\\\". Use when reading or editing any .ts or .tsx file.\\npaths: [\\\"**/*.ts\\\", \\\"**/*.tsx\\\"]\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# TypeScript best practices\\n\\nApply the **type-system-discipline** principle skill first.\\n\\n| Rule | Summary |\\n|------|---------|\\n| Discriminated unions | Model variants with a `kind` literal discriminant so impossible states can't be represented. Validate once at the boundary. |\\n| Constructive modeling | Build the shape so the illegal value can't be constructed. `[T, ...T[]]` for non-empty, `[T, T][]` for even length, `start` plus `duration` for a range. Not a runtime guard, not a wish for refinement types. |\\n| Simplest total type | Keep `T[]` while every operation on it stays total. Strengthen to `NonEmpty<T>` only where the loose type forces `!`, a cast, or a \\\"should never happen\\\" throw. |\\n| `unknown` over `any` | External data is `unknown`. |\\n| Schemas before guards | Before hand-writing a property-by-property type guard, use the repository's runtime schema library and infer the type from the schema, such as `z.infer`. |\\n| No `as` casts | Every `as` is a runtime crash waiting. Cast only after validation. |\\n| Narrowing hierarchy | Discriminant switch > `in` operator > `typeof`/`instanceof` > user-defined type guard > `as`. |\\n| Type guards | Must verify the claim. A lying guard is worse than `as` because the bug hides behind a name that says it's safe. Name them `isX` or `hasX`. |\\n| Exhaustiveness | Inline `const _exhaustive: never = x;` in default arms so the compiler errors when a new variant is added. |\\n| `satisfies` over `as` | Validates the value without widening literal types. |\\n| Boundary validation | Parse where data crosses in, into a named domain type. `Record<string, unknown>` (however spelled) stops at that parse. Trust types inside. See the **boundary-discipline** principle skill. |\\n| Schema-derived types | Reach for `Pick`/`Omit`/`Parameters`/`ReturnType`/`Awaited`/`typeof` before declaring a new interface. |\\n| Object args | Pass objects, not positional, so argument order is self-documenting. Skip on hot paths (per-frame render, tokenizers, parsers). |\\n| Real tests | Don't mock what you can run. Prefer the framework's real test primitives with leak/disposable checks, and verify UI in a running build. Mock only what you can't run locally. |\\n| Structured telemetry | Prefer structured logger diagnostics with enough context to debug from an id. No `console.log` in shipped code. |\\n\\nExamples: `references/patterns.md`.\\n\\n## Session capabilities and permissions\\n\\nRead [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) for the current session. Read the [type-system-discipline](../principle-type-system-discipline/SKILL.md) principle first, and the [boundary-discipline](../principle-boundary-discipline/SKILL.md) principle for boundary validation. Use the complete [patterns reference](references/patterns.md). If a dependency cannot be read, name it and label the review partial.\\n\\nApply these practices to supplied code or readable repository files. Saved edits require available write tools and authorization for the affected paths. If writes are denied or unavailable, return a proposed refactor in the conversation and state that it is unsaved. If no TypeScript input can be read or supplied, report the missing input before proceeding.\\n\\nRun the repository's checks only with available execution tools and authorized commands. Reuse its installed runtime schema library; do not install a dependency for one guard. Report compiler, test, and running UI checks only after observing their results. If execution is denied or unavailable, identify the checks that remain unperformed. Retain the source metadata without assuming that every host enforces paths or disable-model-invocation.\\n\"},\"limit\":\"Read after two small Bun audit scripts had already been written; those scripts do not implement the cache API.\"}\n"

      "text": "import assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { writeFile, mkdir } from 'node:fs/promises';\nimport { resolve } from 'node:path';\nconst out = import.meta.dir;\nconst root = resolve(out, '../..');\nconst receipts = [];\nawait mkdir(resolve(out, 'receipts'), { recursive: true });\nfunction run(name, args, expectedExit, expectedText) {\n  const result = Bun.spawnSync(['bun', '--no-install', ...args], { cwd: root });\n  const stdout = result.stdout.toString();\n  const stderr = result.stderr.toString();\n  const receipt = { name, command: ['bun', '--no-install', ...args], cwd: root, exitCode: result.exitCode, stdout, stderr, expectedExit, expectedText };\n  receipts.push(receipt);\n  return writeFile(resolve(out, `receipts/${String(receipts.length).padStart(2, '0')}-${name}.json`), JSON.stringify(receipt, null, 2)).then(() => {\n    assert.equal(result.exitCode, expectedExit);\n    assert.ok(stdout.includes(expectedText), name);\n    console.log(JSON.stringify(receipt));\n  });\n}\nawait run('supplied-after-state-teardown-throws', ['input/probe.mjs'], 1, 'teardown error: TypeError:');\nawait run('restored-timer-before-state-reports-true', ['outputs/candidate-b/before/probe.mjs'], 0, 'disposed ready: true');\nawait writeFile(resolve(out, 'baseline-receipts.json'), JSON.stringify(receipts, null, 2));\n"

      "text": "import assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { get, put, invalidate } from './repair/cache.mjs';\nimport { mount } from './repair/caller.mjs';\nconst flush = () => new Promise(resolve => queueMicrotask(resolve));\nconst name = process.argv[2];\nif (name === 'immediate-invalidation') {\n  put('direct', { ready: false });\n  assert.equal(get('direct').ready, false);\n  invalidate('direct');\n  assert.equal(get('direct'), undefined);\n  const reports = [];\n  const unmount = mount('immediate', value => reports.push(value));\n  assert.equal(get('immediate').ready, true);\n  unmount();\n  assert.equal(get('immediate'), undefined);\n  assert.deepEqual(reports, []);\n  await flush();\n  assert.deepEqual(reports, [true]);\n  console.log('direct=false then absent; mount=true then immediately absent; report=[true]');\n} else if (name === 'repeated-teardown') {\n  const reports = [];\n  const unmount = mount('repeat', value => reports.push(value));\n  assert.equal(get('repeat').ready, true);\n  unmount();\n  unmount();\n  await flush();\n  unmount();\n  await flush();\n  assert.deepEqual(reports, [true]);\n  assert.equal(get('repeat'), undefined);\n  console.log('report=[true]; repeated teardown leaves absent');\n} else if (name === 'same-key-remount') {\n  const reports = [];\n  const oldUnmount = mount('same', value => reports.push(['old', value]));\n  const newUnmount = mount('same', value => reports.push(['new', value]));\n  const replacement = get('same');\n  oldUnmount();\n  assert.equal(get('same'), replacement);\n  assert.equal(get('same').ready, true);\n  await flush();\n  assert.deepEqual(reports, [['old', true]]);\n  assert.equal(get('same').ready, true);\n  newUnmount();\n  const thirdUnmount = mount('same', value => reports.push(['third', value]));\n  newUnmount();\n  assert.equal(get('same').ready, true);\n  await flush();\n  assert.deepEqual(reports, [['old', true], ['new', true]]);\n  thirdUnmount();\n  await flush();\n  assert.deepEqual(reports, [['old', true], ['new', true], ['third', true]]);\n  const oldRelease = put('replacement', { ready: true });\n  put('replacement', { ready: false });\n  oldRelease();\n  assert.equal(get('replacement').ready, false);\n  const shared = { ready: true };\n  const sharedRelease = put('shared', shared);\n  put('shared', shared);\n  sharedRelease();\n  assert.equal(get('shared').ready, true);\n  console.log('old report=true; remount survives; distinct replacement=false; reused value survives');\n} else if (name === 'separate-key-isolation') {\n  const reports = [];\n  const stopA = mount('a', value => reports.push(['a', value]));\n  const stopB = mount('b', value => reports.push(['b', value]));\n  assert.equal(get('a').ready, true);\n  assert.equal(get('b').ready, true);\n  stopA();\n  assert.equal(get('a'), undefined);\n  assert.equal(get('b').ready, true);\n  await flush();\n  assert.deepEqual(reports, [['a', true]]);\n  stopB();\n  await flush();\n  assert.deepEqual(reports, [['a', true], ['b', true]]);\n  assert.equal(get('b'), undefined);\n  console.log('a absent while b=true; reports=[[a,true],[b,true]]');\n} else if (name === 'callback-failure') {\n  let caught;\n  let calls = 0;\n  process.once('uncaughtException', error => { caught = error; });\n  const stop = mount('throws', () => { calls++; throw new Error('report failed'); });\n  assert.equal(get('throws').ready, true);\n  stop();\n  assert.equal(get('throws'), undefined);\n  const nextStop = mount('throws', () => {});\n  await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 5));\n  assert.equal(caught?.message, 'report failed');\n  stop();\n  await flush();\n  assert.equal(calls, 1);\n  assert.equal(get('throws').ready, true);\n  nextStop();\n  await flush();\n  console.log('error=report failed; calls=1; replacement=true; cleanup completed');\n} else { throw new Error('unknown check'); }\n"
    },

      "path": "strict-method-repairs/arena-walkthrough/outputs/candidate-b/checklist.md",

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "# Candidate B checklist\n\nLocal Markdown is the reduced todo binding. The initial checklist was created before task reads. The verbatim selected playbook steps follow before task-specific todos. This worker owns the candidate implementation directly under the no-nested-agent assignment exception.\n\n- [x] 1. Reproduce it yourself on the matching surface via the control skill in the mode's Non-negotiables, even when a debug or instrumentation protocol says to ask the user to reproduce. Ask the user only with a stated, specific reason the control surface cannot reach the target, and only after driving it as far as it goes. If it won't reproduce directly, synthesize the trigger, tighten conditions, or instrument until it fires. Record the exact symptom, trigger, surface, revision, command or action, exit status where available, and output before changing production code. Missing control companions or denied execution leave the original reproduction unverified. A proxy check cannot satisfy the matching-surface gate.\n\n- [x] 2. Binary-search the cause. Form candidate hypotheses, then rule them out until one survives. Seed them with [how](../../how/SKILL.md) over the affected subsystem and [why](../../why/SKILL.md) for regression history, using their complete prompts and source contracts. Each pass takes the split that cuts the most remaining problem space, gets runtime evidence and eliminates candidates. When program state is unclear, add authorized instrumentation or logging and read it as the code runs. Don't guess. Drive a long or stubborn hunt with an exposed, authorized repeated-execution operation. If unavailable, perform bounded in-session iterations and disclose reduced capability, without claiming a background loop. Confirm the surviving mechanism with runtime evidence before the step-3 architect/interrogate fan-out.\n\n- [x] 3. Plan the fix. If it crosses a function boundary, [architect](../../architect/SKILL.md) first, using its complete exploration, runner, rationale and screening contracts. Contested design follows the mode's [interrogate](../../interrogate/SKILL.md) gate. Delegate implementation to a subagent using the configured bug-fix role with a specific scope. The portable default is inherited model and effort. The canonical default `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` is historical provenance, not current availability. Select a configured model only when supported by exposed tools and observed; retain rejected selections and disclosed fallbacks. Unknown actual models prove no diversity. No required independent operation means that gate remains blocked.\n\n- [x] 4. Verify on the same surface. The original repro now passes. Retain the same trigger and conditions and record the actual output after the bounded root-cause fix. \"Inconclusive\" or wrong-surface is not a pass. Flag it. Unit tests show branch behavior, not bug absence. Keep denied controls, missing companions and unrun checks explicit.\n\n- [ ] 5. Stage the commits so the failing repro lands before the fix in git history. See [tdd](../../tdd/SKILL.md) for the failing-test-first cadence when the bug has a cheap local test path. Skip adding that test when it would be expensive, integration-heavy or unclear, and state the reason and closest executable regression check. This is the canonical [sequence-verifiable-units](../../principle-sequence-verifiable-units/SKILL.md) principle skill, the failing test first and the fix on top. Commits, rebases and history changes require actual authorization and available operations. Without them, preserve the failing-before/passing-after artifacts and ordered delivery plan; do not claim that sequence landed.\n  skip: Commits and history changes are forbidden. Ordered failure and repair receipts are retained.\n\n- [ ] 6. Run [Opening a PR](opening-a-pr.md) in full when its dependency and required capabilities are available and authorized. Missing playbook or companion gates stop dependent delivery. Return checked local artifacts and the exact unperformed actions otherwise. PR creation and other external writes require explicit authorization. Opening a PR does not implicitly start Babysit.\n  skip: External actions and PRs are forbidden. Parent owns integration and review.\n\n## Architect phases\n\n- [x] Ground\n- [x] Sketch\n- [x] Agree. No opt-in checkpoint and isolated implementation is authorized. Parent synthesis remains separate.\n- [x] Implement\n- [x] Scrap. Not needed. The implementation follows the sketch.\n\n## Throughput checkpoint\n\n- Blocking first steps. Checklist, required full reads, revision verification, then original failure and before-state comparison.\n- Independent workstreams. This candidate owns its directory. Parent owns all other candidates, judgment and synthesis. No nested work is authorized.\n- Shared mutable state. No output writes cross the candidate directory. The runtime map is the single current-value index. Mounts keep independent disposal values and conditional release ownership.\n- Smallest safe decomposition. One owner implements this small two-module repair and tests it directly. Parent provides review separation.\n\n## Task-specific work\n\n- [x] Read all seven input files end to end and required frozen-package sources and principle leaves.\n- [x] Read exact method and immutable assignment.\n- [x] Write caller usage before type sketch and implementation.\n- [x] Preserve raw failure, seven ordered checks and callback-failure supplement.\n- [x] Screen design and inspect the repair diff.\n- [x] Verify exact vendor pin, unchanged repaired probe and input revision.\n- [x] Apply unslop to the explanation.\n- [x] Write non-self-referential result last.\n\n## Limits\n\nNested how explorers and implementation delegates are forbidden. How was applied directly and read-only during grounding. This candidate is one parent-owned Arena runner, with no claim of an independently judged synthesis. The matching control-cli companion and create-skill companion are not exposed here. Direct Bun execution verifies the actual supplied CLI fixture, but does not establish those companion gates. No separate Comment Sicko or no-comments review ran. No deslop, commit, PR, installation, public dependency validation, external history investigation or external action ran. Parent review and integration remain outstanding.\n"

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "# Design screening\n\nThe release closure hides generation comparison without adding public tokens. Cache identity stays private. The mount owns its immutable disposal value and schedules one callback. There are no pass-through modules or hand-synchronized registries. The two-module call chain keeps map policy in the cache and callback policy in the caller.\n\nThe raw fixture still permits external key invalidation while a mount lives. That operation removes lookup visibility but does not destroy the mount-owned disposal value. This is intentional.\n\nDiff inspection found one representation change in cache.mjs and one lifetime repair in caller.mjs. The vendored disposer and repaired probe hashes match input. Report errors propagate, and the supplemental check observes the exact report failed error while a same-key replacement survives.\n\nThis is a self-screen, not an independent review. The parent owns acceptance and synthesis.\n"

      "text": "import { mount } from './caller.mjs';\nlet error;\nprocess.once('uncaughtException', caught => { error = caught; });\nconst unmount = mount('fixture-key', ready => console.log('disposed ready:', ready));\nunmount();\nawait new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 5));\nconsole.log(error ? `teardown error: ${error.name}: ${error.message}` : 'teardown completed');\nprocess.exitCode = error ? 1 : 0;\n"

    {
      "path": "strict-method-repairs/arena-walkthrough/outputs/candidate-b/before/caller.mjs",
      "bytes": 309,
      "sha256": "9566a520d6763d359c4b43cd5705df6333c8bf4a4afb96aec7ac3ca2e2145490",
      "owner": "local-013-strict-arena-walkthrough",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import { createDisposer } from './vendor/disposer-v1.mjs';\nimport { get, put, invalidate } from './cache.mjs';\nexport function mount(key, report) {\n  put(key, { ready: true });\n  const subscription = createDisposer(() => report(get(key).ready));\n  return () => { subscription.dispose(); invalidate(key); };\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "strict-method-repairs/arena-walkthrough/outputs/candidate-b/before/cache.mjs",
      "bytes": 220,
      "sha256": "b9ff3cf490c78675ef169324135630dcd5741dbd031de81d2798f7c67c020dea",
      "owner": "local-013-strict-arena-walkthrough",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "const entries = new Map();\nexport function put(key, value) { entries.set(key, value); }\nexport function get(key) { return entries.get(key); }\nexport function invalidate(key) { setTimeout(() => entries.delete(key), 0); }\n"
    },

      "path": "strict-method-repairs/arena-walkthrough/outputs/candidate-b/proposal.md",
      "bytes": 8245,
      "sha256": "2cd5e7a62c35445a95b117c4a955d434b0f9daea86f1d4fde468e4f7d22ede9a",

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "# Cache entries belong to mounts\n\n## Problem\n\nSynchronous invalidation removes the cache entry before the vendored disposal microtask reads it. The supplied after-state throws. The restored timer passes because the microtask reads before the timer deletes. Keep immediate invalidation and make teardown independent of the cache's current value. All claims concern the seven supplied files and the pinned local disposer only.\n\n## Usage (caller's view)\n\nThe consumer keeps the current `mount` contract. Unmount removes its current entry immediately and reports its own ready value once the disposal microtask runs.\n\n```js\nimport { mount } from './caller.mjs';\nimport { get } from './cache.mjs';\nconst unmount = mount('panel', ready => console.log(ready));\nunmount();\nconsole.log(get('panel')); // undefined\n// The deferred report receives true.\n```\n\nA replacement survives the previous mount's teardown.\n\n```js\nconst oldUnmount = mount('panel', ready => console.log('old', ready));\nconst newUnmount = mount('panel', ready => console.log('new', ready));\noldUnmount();\nconsole.log(get('panel').ready); // true\nnewUnmount();\n```\n\nDirect cache writers receive a release function that removes only the entry they installed. Administrative invalidation still deletes the current entry by key immediately.\n\n```js\nimport { put, get, invalidate } from './cache.mjs';\nconst releaseOld = put('panel', { ready: true });\nput('panel', { ready: false });\nreleaseOld();\nconsole.log(get('panel').ready); // false\ninvalidate('panel');\nconsole.log(get('panel')); // undefined\n```\n\n## Shape\n\n`Map<string, { value: Ready }>` owns current entries. Each `put` allocates a fresh private wrapper and returns a release closure bound to that wrapper. The closure compares entry identity before deleting. A repeated release is harmless. Value identity alone is insufficient because writers may reuse the same value object.\n\nThe mount owns a frozen `{ ready: true }` value and its release function. Its disposal callback reads that value directly. Its teardown guard prevents repeated scheduling. A `finally` releases the entry if scheduling throws synchronously. A report failure stays observable as an uncaught callback error. Cache cleanup has already completed before the deferred callback executes.\n\nThe public cache has the existing three functions. `put` gains a useful return value. The release closure hides generation identity and comparison rules. Callers still own when to release and their callback-error policy. This is a smaller interface than exposing tokens or a disposal queue.\n\n```ts\ntype Ready = Readonly<{ ready: boolean }>;\ntype Release = () => void;\nexport function put(key: string, value: Ready): Release;\nexport function get(key: string): Ready | undefined;\nexport function invalidate(key: string): void;\nexport function mount(key: string, report: (ready: boolean) => void): Release;\n```\n\n`cache.mjs` owns the map and entry identity. `caller.mjs` owns mount lifetime and the report callback. `vendor/disposer-v1.mjs` stays byte-for-byte unchanged. No new module or transport types are needed.\n\nThe preimplementation signatures and boundaries are in `design-sketch.mjs`. The executable implementation is in `repair/`.\n\n## Read-only architecture explanation\n\n### Overview\n\nThe supplied cache is one module-scoped map. `mount` writes a ready object and returns an unmount function. `createDisposer` schedules its callback through `queueMicrotask` on every `dispose` call.\n\n### How it works\n\n`caller.mjs` first calls `put`. It creates a callback that later performs `get(key).ready`. Unmount calls `dispose`, which queues rather than executes the callback. Unmount then calls `invalidate`, which deletes synchronously. Once the stack completes, the queued callback dereferences `undefined`. This is deterministic event-loop ordering rather than simultaneous threaded execution.\n\nWith the removed timer restored, invalidation schedules a timer instead. The disposal microtask runs first and sees the entry. The timer hides the lifetime coupling while delaying the promised invalidation. It also risks deleting a replacement installed before the timer fires.\n\n### Where things live\n\n`input/cache.mjs` owns storage. `input/caller.mjs` owns subscription setup and teardown. `input/vendor/disposer-v1.mjs` determines scheduling. `input/probe.mjs` observes uncaught teardown errors. `input/invalidation.diff` shows the ordering change. `input/manifest.json` pins the exact local dependency. `input/README.md` defines the limited dependency claim.\n\n### Gotchas\n\nA missing-entry guard would suppress the crash but lose the required true report. A callback that reads the current key can accidentally observe the next mount. Repeated unmount currently queues repeated callbacks. Capturing the old value alone does not prevent an old teardown from deleting a new entry.\n\n## Synthesis decision\n\nThis is candidate B, not the parent synthesis. No peer artifacts or rubric were read. Parent selection, grafting, independent judgment and synthesis verification remain parent-owned.\n\n## Tradeoffs accepted\n\n- We accept one wrapper per `put` and one release closure in exchange for replacement-safe cleanup without exposed tokens.\n- We accept retaining the mount value until its callback runs in exchange for a truthful report after immediate invalidation.\n- We accept propagation of report exceptions in exchange for preserving the fixture's error visibility. This change adds no logging or swallowing policy.\n- We accept one local boolean per mount in exchange for an exactly-once report under repeated teardown.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n1. Snapshot plus unconditional `invalidate(key)` has the smallest source edit, but an old mount can delete a new mount. Its interface hides too little ownership policy.\n2. A cache-managed lease object with `read`, `close`, and `onDispose` could hide the whole lifecycle. It expands a three-function cache into a subscription framework and duplicates the vendored scheduling boundary.\n3. A deferred invalidation timer keeps the callback working but fails immediate visibility and can delete a newer entry. An `await dispose()` API also changes callers while the supplied disposer returns no completion signal.\n\nThe first two sketches are structurally distinct. They were compared before implementation, with the ownership-aware release closure chosen for the supplied scope. They are design sketches, not separately executed prototypes.\n\n## Principles and decisions\n\n- Model the Domain and Foundational Thinking put entry generations in fresh private wrappers before logic was written.\n- Separate Before Serializing Shared State gives each mount its own disposal value and entry ownership. No lock is needed for the single-threaded map.\n- Make Operations Idempotent gives teardown one transition and release a conditional delete.\n- Boundary Discipline keeps report-error policy at the caller and leaves the disposer unchanged.\n- Encode Lessons in Structure enforces replacement safety through the release closure rather than a comment telling callers to check ownership.\n- Laziness Protocol and Minimize Reader Load preserve two implementation modules and avoid a scheduler abstraction.\n- Exhaust the Design Space compares value capture, cache-managed leases and deferred deletion before selecting the proposal.\n- Test Behavior, Not Implementation and Prove It Works retain observable true and false values, exact teardown failures, and rerunnable receipts against real files.\n\n## Open questions and risks\n\nCould future mount values become mutable after setup? This fixture creates a frozen ready object. A richer caller must decide whether disposal reports its mount value or a teardown-time snapshot.\n\nShould application code recover from report errors? This candidate preserves their uncaught visibility. Recovery needs an explicit application contract.\n\nHistorical motivation beyond the supplied diff is unknown. No external dependency, issue, chat or deployment evidence was authorized or consulted.\n\n## Next implementation step\n\nAfter parent synthesis, port the selected repair from the isolated candidate directory and rerun `bun --no-install outputs/candidate-b/verify-repair.mjs` with the selected implementation paths.\n"

      "text": "import { createDisposer } from './vendor/disposer-v1.mjs';\nimport { put } from './cache.mjs';\nexport function mount(key, report) {\n  const value = Object.freeze({ ready: true });\n  const release = put(key, value);\n  const subscription = createDisposer(() => report(value.ready));\n  let disposed = false;\n  return () => {\n    if (disposed) return;\n    disposed = true;\n    try { subscription.dispose(); }\n    finally { release(); }\n  };\n}\n"

      "text": "const entries = new Map();\nexport function put(key, value) {\n  const entry = { value };\n  entries.set(key, entry);\n  return () => {\n    if (entries.get(key) === entry) entries.delete(key);\n  };\n}\nexport function get(key) { return entries.get(key)?.value; }\nexport function invalidate(key) { entries.delete(key); }\n"

    {
      "path": "strict-method-repairs/arena-walkthrough/outputs/parent-comparison.md",
      "bytes": 3288,
      "sha256": "6ba298fa3d63c49e3d03d63054121ea19da63e83f7c203a61adc915181a05c13",
      "owner": "local-013-strict-arena-walkthrough",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "# Parent criterion comparison\n\nThese scores compare candidate designs against the withheld rubric. They do not grade this workflow.\n\n| Criterion | A | B | Parent rationale |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Causal accuracy | 4 | 4 | Both proposals trace the actual queueMicrotask callback, synchronous deletion and restored timer behavior. The recorded failure is the supplied probe, not a mock. |\n| Caller contract and state ownership | 4 | 4 | Both retain mount-specific values and return release closures from put. Fresh wrapper identity protects replacements even when the same value object is reused. Parent probes confirm both remount orderings and idempotence. |\n| Failure handling | 4 | 4 | Both release in finally, schedule at most once and preserve observable report exceptions. Candidate supplements and parent callback-failure probes confirm cleanup and single reporting. |\n| Verification quality | 4 | 4 | Both retain the seven ordered observations and callback failure. Parent reran actual probes and behavior checks without modifying candidate output. A tests explicit release of the later same-object publication. B asserts the callback has not run synchronously before flushing. |\n| Extension and maintenance cost | 4 | 4 | Both use two runtime modules and a private wrapper behind three cache functions. Both reject timer restoration, unconditional stale deletion and a lifecycle framework. B freezes its ready object; A retains the fixture's mutability policy. This is a minor policy difference, not a separate architecture. |\n\nTotals are 20 for each. Prefer A provisionally because it preserves the fixture's value mutability and has no extra freeze policy. This is a tie-break within genuine architectural convergence, not evidence that B is incorrect. Revisit this decision against the independent judge before integration.\n\nThe complete candidate sources, rationale and checks were read after their terminal notifications. Result identity, revision and method checks are in inspection-a.json and inspection-b.json. Parent execution is in parent-candidate-a-receipts.json and parent-candidate-b-receipts.json. The parent does not rerun receipt-writing worker orchestration inside worker-owned directories.\n\nA red-flag screen finds one map owner, mount-local retained values, a private identity check and no forwarding module. Owner release and force invalidation express different authority. Their coexistence is deliberate.\n\n## Judge resolution\n\nThe judge scored A 20 and B 19, subtracting one point from B's caller-contract criterion for its added freeze. The parent initially treated this as a harmless policy difference and scored B 20. A direct mutation comparison in mutation-receipts.json confirms observable divergence. A accepts the assignment and reports false. B throws TypeError and reports true. The parent accepts the judge's criterion-2 deduction. Final comparison is A 20 and B 19. Both recommend A. No disagreement about the ownership architecture remains.\n\nThe judge also correctly identifies B's hardcoded, overwrite-prone runner. It is rejected as the synthesis runner. The new synthesis runner targets actual synthesis files and preserves every receipt. The loser implementation and screening rationale were reread after judgment before integration.\n"

      "text": "import assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';\nimport { resolve } from 'node:path';\nconst dir = resolve(process.argv[2]);\nconst { mount } = await import(pathToFileURL(dir + '/caller.mjs'));\nconst { get } = await import(pathToFileURL(dir + '/cache.mjs'));\nlet calls = 0;\nlet caught;\nprocess.once('uncaughtException', error => { caught = error; });\nconst stop = mount('throws', () => { calls++; throw new Error('report failed'); });\nstop();\nassert.equal(get('throws'), undefined);\nawait new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 5));\nassert.equal(caught?.message, 'report failed');\nstop();\nawait new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 5));\nassert.equal(calls, 1);\nconsole.log(JSON.stringify({ error: caught.message, calls, deletedImmediately: true }));\n"
