      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "# Synthesis decision and evidence\n\nCandidate A is the base. It preserves synchronous invalidation and mutable fixture values while retaining a mount's callback state independently. Both candidates independently chose private publication wrappers and release closures that delete only their own publication. No implementation graft is needed for this genuine convergence.\n\nThe judge recommended A with scores 20 and 19. The parent initially scored both 20. Mutation probes confirmed that B's Object.freeze adds a caller-visible TypeError, so the parent accepts the judge's one-point deduction under caller contract. All other criteria remain equal. These are proposal comparisons, not a workflow grade. Full rationales are in ../parent-comparison.md and ../judge/RESULT.JSON.\n\nCandidate B contributes an explicit empty-report assertion immediately after teardown, followed by a true report after the microtask. It also contributes the overlapping-mount example in proposal.md. Both were adapted into the existing ownership design. A's tests already cover repeated teardown, publication replacement with a reused object, separate keys and callback errors.\n\nB's freeze policy is rejected because the task does not require immutable values. Its receipt runner is rejected because it hardcodes candidate paths, reuses baseline receipts and overwrites prior receipt files. Restoring a deletion timer is rejected because it delays invalidation and can remove a replacement. Missing-entry guards and success fallbacks would conceal a lost report. A lifecycle framework would expand this small cache without a supplied need. There were no candidate dropouts or metadata retries.\n\nThe synthesized implementation was inspected and executed from actual files. ../synthesis-verification.json records seven ordered primary observations, callback failure, parent lifecycle probes and the mutable-value contract. The original probe still exits 1. The restored timer and repaired probe exit 0 and report true. All remaining commands exit 0 and contain literal behavior assertions in their test files. The vendored disposer hash matches input/manifest.json. This is evidence for the exact local fixture only.\n\nThe same rubric was checked on the synthesis. Its causal explanation uses the real microtask ordering. The unchanged mount API and publication-specific releases preserve caller ownership. Callback exceptions remain visible after cleanup. The runner executes real files and preserves prior receipts. The implementation stays in two modules, with fresh private identity and mount-local state. No numeric workflow score or host pass is awarded.\n\n## Principles and concrete decisions\n\n- Separate Before Serializing Shared State gives each candidate a directory and each mount its own retained callback value.\n- Laziness Protocol retains A's smaller behavioral change and rejects freezing, timers and lifecycle-framework expansion.\n- Redesign From First Principles integrates B's timing assertion and usage into one publication-ownership model.\n- Prove It Works requires parent reruns against actual candidate and synthesis files.\n- Model the Domain uses private publication wrappers instead of scattered stale-owner checks.\n- Foundational Thinking defines current publication versus retained mount value before logic.\n- Build the Lever produces verify.mjs and the independent probes for repeatable inspection.\n- Test Behavior, Not Implementation checks true and false reports, actual lookup values, replacement identity and literal callback failures.\n- Sequence Work into Verifiable Units preserves original failure, restored-before behavior and repaired behavior in that order.\n- Boundary Discipline preserves the supplied callback-error boundary instead of swallowing exceptions.\n- Make Operations Idempotent marks teardown before scheduling and makes stale release harmless.\n- Minimize Reader Load keeps cache policy and caller lifetime in the two existing modules.\n- Encode Lessons in Structure prevents stale deletion with private publication identity rather than a caller convention.\n- Fix Root Causes retains mount state instead of masking absent cache reads.\n- Exhaust the Design Space compares independently produced proposals and their whole-shape alternatives before selection.\n\n## Attention\n\nreviewed by unknown\n\n- Version 0.1.3 was observed in the supplied cache. Its freeze SHA cannot be independently established because the directory has no Git metadata. The supplied freeze is recorded without claiming confirmation.\n- Direct source reads establish access, not installed discovery.\n- Output directories were created after candidate bootstrap, though before immutable assignment and work dispatch. This differs from the requested bootstrap ordering.\n- An identity check inadvertently opened the package's historical tested-package marker. Its report-path listing was seen. No referenced old output or prior grade was opened or used. Exact details are in ../initial-limitations.md.\n- Full native transcript export is unavailable. Selected actual tool return payloads and execution outputs are retained. The judge's failed ArrayBuffer digest attempt is disclosed in its result, but its raw tool output is not available to the parent. No complete transcript audit is claimed.\n- Actual models and efforts are unknown. Verified cross-model trail review is unavailable. Distinct worker identities do not prove model diversity.\n- create-skill, no-comments and matching control companions were not executed. How and Why roles within candidates were performed directly under the no-nested-worker restriction. Their independent companion gates remain unproven.\n- Report values remain mutable. Disposal reads the retained object's current state rather than a deep snapshot. A synchronous disposer scheduling failure was not simulated because the dependency is the exact pinned queueMicrotask implementation.\n- The supplied strict-schema reference ends inside an unclosed Python try block. The first execution attempt failed with SyntaxError and is preserved in ../structural-attempt-0.json and ../strict-method-attempt-0.py. The second execution retained every supplied check and added only a closing rethrow handler and return of collected errors. It reported no structural relationship errors. This execution shim does not judge qualitative success.\n"

      "text": "import assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { put, get } from '../cache.mjs';\nimport { mount } from '../caller.mjs';\nconst reports = [];\nconst old = mount('key', value => reports.push(['old', value]));\nold();\nconst next = mount('key', value => reports.push(['next', value]));\nawait Promise.resolve();\nassert.equal(get('key').ready, true);\nassert.deepEqual(reports, [['old', true]]);\nold();\nassert.equal(get('key').ready, true);\nput('key', { ready: false });\nnext();\nawait Promise.resolve();\nassert.equal(get('key').ready, false);\nassert.deepEqual(reports, [['old', true], ['next', true]]);\nconst stale = mount('overlap', value => reports.push(['stale', value]));\nconst current = mount('overlap', value => reports.push(['current', value]));\nstale();\nassert.equal(get('overlap').ready, true);\nawait Promise.resolve();\ncurrent();\nawait Promise.resolve();\nassert.deepEqual(reports, [['old', true], ['next', true], ['stale', true], ['current', true]]);\nassert.equal(get('overlap'), undefined);\nconst value = { ready: false };\nconst releaseOld = put('same-object', value);\nconst releaseNew = put('same-object', value);\nreleaseOld();\nassert.equal(get('same-object').ready, false);\nreleaseNew();\nassert.equal(get('same-object'), undefined);\nconsole.log('remount ready: true; replacement ready: false; overlap reports: true,true; same-object preserved: false');\n"

    {
      "path": "strict-method-repairs/arena-walkthrough/outputs/synthesis/proposal.md",
      "bytes": 2876,
      "sha256": "4b38e1624e61766c2641996217827731d071dee3d8d5fac564e7af0609ad2de9",

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "# Release the publication a mount owns\n\nA caller can invalidate immediately and still report its mount value when disposal runs later. `put` returns a release closure that cannot delete a newer publication. The existing `mount(key, report)` API remains unchanged.\n\n```js\nconst stop = mount('panel', ready => console.log(ready));\nstop();\nconsole.log(get('panel')); // undefined now; deferred report receives true\n```\n\nOverlapping mounts retain separate cleanup authority. This usage adapts candidate B's overlapping-mount example.\n\n```js\nconst stopOld = mount('panel', ready => console.log('old', ready));\nconst stopNew = mount('panel', ready => console.log('new', ready));\nstopOld();\nconsole.log(get('panel').ready); // true, the new publication remains\nstopNew();\n```\n\nThe cache owns `Map<Key, { value }>` and allocates a private wrapper for every publication. `get` unwraps the current value. `invalidate` deletes the current key synchronously. Owner release deletes only the wrapper that created it. Even publishing the same value object twice creates separate cleanup authority.\n\nThe mount retains its object for the deferred callback. It marks teardown once before scheduling and releases in `finally`. A callback error remains observable after immediate cleanup. The pinned disposer remains unchanged.\n\n```ts\ntype Release = () => void;\ninterface Cache<K, V> {\n  put(key: K, value: V): Release;\n  get(key: K): V | undefined;\n  invalidate(key: K): void;\n}\n```\n\nThe supplied failure comes from reading current cache state in a queued microtask after synchronous deletion. Restoring the old timer hides that lifetime mismatch and can delete a replacement. Retaining a mount value and publication-specific release fixes both problems without adding a scheduler or lease framework.\n\nThe retained object is mutable, as in the supplied fixture. Disposal reports that object's current `ready` value. It is not a deep snapshot. Force invalidation removes lookup visibility while a live mount can still report its retained state. Recovery from report exceptions requires an application contract beyond this fixture.\n\nCandidate A supplies the base. Both candidates converged on this ownership design. Candidate B contributes the explicit deferred-report test and the overlapping-mount usage. Its additional freeze policy is rejected because mutation was not prohibited by the task. Timers, missing-entry success fallbacks and a lifecycle framework are also rejected.\n\nRun `bun --no-install outputs/synthesis/verify.mjs` from the task root. Every run writes a new receipt. The original seven observations run in order, followed by callback failure, parent lifecycle checks and the explicit mutation contract. This verifies the exact local vendored fixture only.\n\nThe adjacent `../synthesis-note.md` records comparison, judge disagreement, source attribution and verification limits.\n"

      "path": "strict-method-repairs/arena-walkthrough/outputs/grounding.md",
      "bytes": 1634,

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "# Cache lifetime problem\n\nThe cache stores values in a module-local Map. put replaces the key, get returns the current value, and invalidate deletes it synchronously. The caller owns a disposer subscription but its callback reads the shared key later.\n\nmount first stores a fresh { ready: true } object. createDisposer returns dispose that schedules onDispose with queueMicrotask. unmount calls dispose and then invalidate in the same stack. Deletion completes before the callback runs, so get(key).ready throws. The supplied Bun probe reproduced this with exit code 1. The local manifest's disposer digest matched the actual vendored bytes.\n\nThe removed setTimeout previously let the queued microtask read the value before the timer deleted it. Restoring a timer would repair this narrow ordering but lets delayed old cleanup delete a replacement under the same key. It also changes the observable invalidation contract.\n\nThe API decision is which owner retains the teardown value. A caller can retain its mounted object instead of looking up mutable current state. A broader cache could issue versioned handles, but it must justify that extra protocol against this fixture. Candidates choose their own shape. The parent rubric is withheld.\n\nThe output is a disposable local proposal and executable repair, with portable evidence for this pinned fixture only. There is no public dependency assertion.\n\nThis direct grounding traces the how explainer format. A separately delegated how explainer was not run. The candidates supply their own independent grounding as part of their Arena artifacts. No independent how review is claimed.\n"

      "text": "# Throughput checkpoint\n\n- Blocking first steps. Read contracts and input, verify SHA, frame task and hide rubric before dispatch.\n- Independent workstreams. Two candidate directories, followed by fresh read-only judge.\n- Shared mutable state. Parent alone owns assignments, events, receipt and synthesis.\n- Smallest safe decomposition. Two independent candidates and one judge satisfy the requested comparison. No nested workers.\n\nAt review boundary, all candidate writes must be terminal and inspected before judge dispatch. At synthesis boundary, parent alone integrates and executes checks.\n\n## Judge boundary\n\nBoth candidates are terminal. Metadata and complete source, rationale and tests were inspected. Parent probes executed with exit 0. A fresh read-only judge was bound and dispatched at event 11. The parent comparison runs while that judge reviews. Shared writes remain parent-owned. No new candidate work is dispatched.\n\n## Synthesis boundary\n\nThe judge is terminal and inspected. Parent accepted its mutation-contract correction after a direct probe. Parent alone wrote the synthesis and executed ten commands, including the seven primary observations. The original failure is retained. No candidate artifacts changed during judging or integration. Receipt validation and final artifact indexing remain parent-owned.\n"

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';\nimport { resolve } from 'node:path';\nconst dir = resolve(process.argv[2]);\nconst { mount } = await import(pathToFileURL(dir + '/caller.mjs'));\nconst { get, put, invalidate } = await import(pathToFileURL(dir + '/cache.mjs'));\nconst flush = () => new Promise(resolve => queueMicrotask(resolve));\nconst observations = [];\nconst report = [];\nconst stop = mount('normal', ready => report.push(ready));\nassert.deepEqual(get('normal'), { ready: true });\nstop();\nassert.equal(get('normal'), undefined);\nawait flush();\nassert.deepEqual(report, [true]);\nobservations.push('teardown reports mounted ready while deletion is immediate');\nstop();\nawait flush();\nassert.deepEqual(report, [true]);\nobservations.push('repeat teardown reports once');\nconst oldReports = [], newReports = [];\nconst oldStop = mount('same', ready => oldReports.push(ready));\nconst newStop = mount('same', ready => newReports.push(ready));\nconst replacement = get('same');\noldStop();\nassert.equal(get('same'), replacement);\nawait flush();\nassert.deepEqual(oldReports, [true]);\nassert.equal(get('same'), replacement);\nnewStop();\nawait flush();\nassert.deepEqual(newReports, [true]);\nassert.equal(get('same'), undefined);\nobservations.push('old unmount after remount preserves replacement');\nconst afterReports = [];\nconst earlierStop = mount('after', value => afterReports.push(value));\nearlierStop();\nconst laterStop = mount('after', value => afterReports.push(value));\nconst laterValue = get('after');\nawait flush();\nassert.equal(get('after'), laterValue);\nlaterStop();\nawait flush();\nassert.deepEqual(afterReports, [true, true]);\nobservations.push('remount after earlier unmount survives deferred callback');\nconst keys = [];\nconst xStop = mount('x', value => keys.push(['x', value]));\nconst yStop = mount('y', value => keys.push(['y', value]));\nxStop();\nassert.deepEqual(get('y'), { ready: true });\nawait flush();\nyStop();\nawait flush();\nassert.deepEqual(keys, [['x', true], ['y', true]]);\nobservations.push('separate keys retain their own reports');\nput('direct', { ready: false });\nassert.deepEqual(get('direct'), { ready: false });\ninvalidate('direct');\nassert.equal(get('direct'), undefined);\nobservations.push('direct invalidation preserves synchronous public contract');\nconsole.log(JSON.stringify({ observations }, null, 2));\n"

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { put, get } from '../repaired/cache.mjs';\nimport { mount } from '../repaired/caller.mjs';\nconst reports = [];\nconst old = mount('key', value => reports.push(['old', value]));\nold();\nconst next = mount('key', value => reports.push(['next', value]));\nawait Promise.resolve();\nassert.equal(get('key').ready, true);\nassert.deepEqual(reports, [['old', true]]);\nold();\nassert.equal(get('key').ready, true);\nput('key', { ready: false });\nnext();\nawait Promise.resolve();\nassert.equal(get('key').ready, false);\nassert.deepEqual(reports, [['old', true], ['next', true]]);\nconst stale = mount('overlap', value => reports.push(['stale', value]));\nconst current = mount('overlap', value => reports.push(['current', value]));\nstale();\nassert.equal(get('overlap').ready, true);\nawait Promise.resolve();\ncurrent();\nawait Promise.resolve();\nassert.deepEqual(reports, [['old', true], ['next', true], ['stale', true], ['current', true]]);\nassert.equal(get('overlap'), undefined);\nconst value = { ready: false };\nconst releaseOld = put('same-object', value);\nconst releaseNew = put('same-object', value);\nreleaseOld();\nassert.equal(get('same-object').ready, false);\nreleaseNew();\nassert.equal(get('same-object'), undefined);\nconsole.log('remount ready: true; replacement ready: false; overlap reports: true,true; same-object preserved: false');\n"
    },

      "text": "import assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { get, put } from '../repaired/cache.mjs';\nimport { mount } from '../repaired/caller.mjs';\nconst errors = [];\nprocess.on('uncaughtException', error => errors.push(error.message));\nlet reports = 0;\nconst bad = mount('bad', ready => {\n  assert.equal(ready, true);\n  reports++;\n  throw Error('report failed');\n});\nbad();\nassert.equal(get('bad'), undefined);\nput('bad', { ready: false });\nawait new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 5));\nbad();\nassert.equal(get('bad').ready, false);\nassert.equal(reports, 1);\nassert.deepEqual(errors, ['report failed']);\nconst goodReports = [];\nconst good = mount('good', ready => goodReports.push(ready));\ngood();\nawait Promise.resolve();\nassert.deepEqual(goodReports, [true]);\nconsole.log('error: report failed; callback count: 1; replacement ready: false; independent report: true');\n"

      "sha256": "ebcf86f8c9da88f71b807ab5314256a4e1fbd97e2dc4b319520d0d51e707a978",
      "owner": "local-013-strict-arena-walkthrough",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import { createDisposer } from './vendor/disposer-v1.mjs';\nimport { put } from './cache.mjs';\nexport function mount(key, report) {\n  const value = { ready: true };\n  const release = put(key, value);\n  const subscription = createDisposer(() => report(value.ready));\n  let disposed = false;\n  return () => {\n    if (disposed) return;\n    disposed = true;\n    try { subscription.dispose(); }\n    finally { release(); }\n  };\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "strict-method-repairs/arena-walkthrough/outputs/candidate-a/repaired/cache.mjs",
      "bytes": 311,
      "sha256": "14bfc2668fd4251d5dc69c571c371a074bb57358b2875635bad3e45b5fc36ef2",
      "owner": "local-013-strict-arena-walkthrough",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "const entries = new Map();\nexport function put(key, value) {\n  const cell = { value };\n  entries.set(key, cell);\n  return () => {\n    if (entries.get(key) === cell) entries.delete(key);\n  };\n}\nexport function get(key) { return entries.get(key)?.value; }\nexport function invalidate(key) { entries.delete(key); }\n"
    },

      "text": "// Exact vendored fixture dependency implementation, pinned by local SHA-256 in manifest.json.\nexport function createDisposer(onDispose) {\n  return { dispose: () => queueMicrotask(onDispose) };\n}\n"
    },

    {
      "path": "strict-method-repairs/arena-walkthrough/outputs/candidate-a/proposal.md",
      "bytes": 9460,
      "sha256": "bb3d96af10430de9fdeffc8bf3cb3432fc06dd7488b4c5b2252518239f232f07",
      "owner": "local-013-strict-arena-walkthrough",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "# Cache teardown with owned publications\n\n## Problem\n\nCache consumers must observe invalidation immediately. A disposed mount must still report its own `ready` value when the vendored disposer invokes its callback in a microtask. The supplied after-state throws in `input/probe.mjs`. The restored timer copy reports `true`. These are observed local results in `baseline-receipts.json`. They establish an ordering regression for this exact fixture, without establishing anything about a public dependency.\n\n## Usage (caller's view)\n\nThe existing `mount(key, report)` call remains unchanged. `put` now returns a release function for that publication. The mount retains its value for its own callback.\n\n```js\nconst unmount = mount('panel', ready => console.log(ready));\nunmount();\n// The cache is absent now. The deferred report receives true.\n```\n\nThe caller publishes one value and owns its release.\n\n```js\nconst value = { ready: true };\nconst release = put(key, value);\nconst subscription = createDisposer(() => report(value.ready));\nlet disposed = false;\nreturn () => {\n\tif (disposed) return;\n\tdisposed = true;\n\ttry { subscription.dispose(); }\n\tfinally { release(); }\n};\n```\n\nAnother publisher can replace the same key safely.\n\n```js\nconst releaseOld = put('panel', { ready: true });\nput('panel', { ready: false });\nreleaseOld();\nconsole.log(get('panel').ready); // false\ninvalidate('panel');\nconsole.log(get('panel')); // undefined immediately\n```\n\n## Shape\n\nThe organizing structure is `Map<Key, Cell<Value>>`. Each `put` allocates a fresh private cell. `get` unwraps the current cell. The returned release closure deletes only when its cell is still current. `invalidate` remains unconditional and synchronous.\n\n```ts\ntype Release = () => void;\ntype Cell<T> = { value: T };\ninterface Cache<K, V> {\n\tput(key: K, value: V): Release;\n\tget(key: K): V | undefined;\n\tinvalidate(key: K): void;\n}\n```\n\nThese are explanatory TypeScript signatures for the supplied JavaScript implementation. The `Cell` type is internal, never exported. The sketch bodies are `put` creates a cell and returns a guarded release, `get` returns the current cell's value, and `invalidate` deletes the current cell. The executable bodies are in `repaired/cache.mjs`.\n\n`repaired/cache.mjs` owns the map and publication identity. `repaired/caller.mjs` owns each mount's retained value, subscription and once-only teardown. `repaired/vendor/disposer-v1.mjs` remains byte-identical to the supplied fixture. `repaired/probe.mjs` remains the actual supplied probe.\n\nThis small interface hides publication comparison inside the cache. The caller retains only domain state and a release function. No timers, generation counters, locks, or transport types cross the boundary. A fresh cell distinguishes replacement even when the same value object is republished.\n\n## How the supplied architecture works\n\n### Overview\n\n`input/cache.mjs` is a module-scoped map. `input/caller.mjs` publishes `{ ready: true }` and arranges for the disposer to report a cache lookup during teardown.\n\n### Key concepts\n\nThe cache represents the current value for a key. A subscription represents deferred cleanup for one mount. The original caller treats those different lifetimes as identical.\n\n### How it works\n\n`mount` writes the value and creates a subscription. Teardown calls `dispose`, which queues the callback with `queueMicrotask`. Teardown then deletes the key synchronously. The callback runs after teardown returns and evaluates `get(key).ready` against the absent entry. The supplied probe captures that uncaught `TypeError` and exits 1.\n\nWith the restored timer, deletion waits until a later timer turn and the queued callback reads `true`. That ordering masks the lifetime mismatch. It also lets consumers see the entry after invalidation and lets an old timer delete a replacement. The chosen repair retains a per-mount value and removes only the owning publication.\n\n### Where things live\n\nThe map and invalidation policy live in `input/cache.mjs`. Mount lifetime lives in `input/caller.mjs`. Deferred dispatch lives in `input/vendor/disposer-v1.mjs`. The probe, diff and manifest describe reproduction, changed timing and fixture identity.\n\n### Gotchas\n\nThis is a deterministic event-loop ordering failure, rather than parallel thread mutation. A callback that throws still escapes the vendored microtask. Cache cleanup has already completed and teardown stays idempotent. This proposal preserves callback error visibility rather than silently reporting success.\n\n## Synthesis decision\n\nThis is candidate A only. The parent chooses the base and any grafts after independent comparison. No peer output or parent rubric was read.\n\n## Tradeoffs accepted\n\n- We accept a private cell allocation per `put` in exchange for exact publication ownership, including same-object replacement.\n- We accept retaining the mount value through its queued callback in exchange for removing cache lifetime dependence.\n- We accept a changed `put` return value in exchange for hiding stale-owner deletion checks from callers. Existing callers can ignore that return value.\n- We accept uncaught callback failures under the supplied disposer contract. They do not roll back invalidation or permit a second report.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n| Shape | Hidden complexity | Exposed complexity | Decision |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Retain value and use unconditional `invalidate(key)` | Deferred callback value lifetime | Caller must coordinate overlapping mounts to avoid removing a replacement | Rejected for stale teardown. |\n| Cache lease with `value`, `release`, `dispose`, and error hooks | Complete lifecycle orchestration | Larger interface couples general cache use to this disposer | Rejected for extension cost. |\n| Current cache plus caller-owned `release` capability | Publication identity and conditional deletion | Mount retains its value and subscription once flag | Chosen. |\n| Restore deletion timer | Event-loop timing | Callers inherit delayed visibility and replacement hazards | Rejected by immediate invalidation requirement. |\n\nThese are distinct design sketches, not independent candidate runs. The parent owns the full Arena competition. The selected design passes the red-flag screen through one map owner, one publication release path, no pass-through modules, and a three-file runtime trace. Legacy force invalidation remains deliberately separate from owner release because the operations have different authority.\n\n## Principles and decisions\n\n`model-the-domain` and `foundational-thinking` make publication identity an explicit private cell before implementation. `separate-before-serializing-shared-state` gives each mount its own callback value and release authority. `make-operations-idempotent` makes teardown report at most once. `boundary-discipline` leaves callback failure visible at the supplied boundary. `laziness-protocol` and `minimize-reader-load` keep the repair in the existing cache and caller. `encode-lessons-in-structure` makes stale release harmless through identity comparison. `exhaust-the-design-space` drives the distinct sketches above. `prove-it-works` and `test-behavior-not-implementation` drive the exact probe and literal observable assertions. Issue tracker, long-form documents, team chat, infrastructure, error tracking, and product analytics were not searched because external actions and unrelated sources are outside this fixture-only assignment. Why exploration and explanation ran sequentially in this worker. Nested agents were forbidden. Preserve immediate invalidation and visible errors. Change mount ownership. Avoid deferral and public-package claims.       "text": "import { mkdir, cp, readFile, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';\nimport { createHash } from 'node:crypto';\nconst root = new URL('./', import.meta.url).pathname;\nconst receipts = [];\nasync function run(name, path, expectedExit, expectedText) {\n  const p = Bun.spawnSync([process.execPath, path], { stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'pipe' });\n  const stdout = p.stdout.toString(), stderr = p.stderr.toString();\n  const passed = p.exitCode === expectedExit && stdout.includes(expectedText);\n  const receipt = {name, command:[process.execPath,path], exitStatus:p.exitCode, stdout, stderr, expectedExit, expectedText, passed};\n  receipts.push(receipt);\n  await writeFile(root + name + '.receipt.json', JSON.stringify(receipt,null,2)+'\\n');\n  if (!passed) throw Error(JSON.stringify(receipt));\n}\nawait run('01-supplied-after-state', root + '../../input/probe.mjs', 1, 'teardown error: TypeError:');\nawait cp(root + '../../input', root + 'before', { recursive:true });\nconst cachePath = root + 'before/cache.mjs';\nconst after = await readFile(cachePath,'utf8');\nawait writeFile(cachePath, after.replace('entries.delete(key);','setTimeout(() => entries.delete(key), 0);'));\nawait run('02-restored-timer-before-state',root+'before/probe.mjs',0,'disposed ready: true\\nteardown completed');\nconst vendor = await readFile(root+'../../input/vendor/disposer-v1.mjs');\nconst manifest = JSON.parse(await readFile(root+'../../input/manifest.json','utf8'));\nconst sha = createHash('sha256').update(vendor).digest('hex');\nif (sha !== manifest.dependency.sha256) throw Error('Vendored disposer digest mismatch');\nawait writeFile(root+'baseline-receipts.json', JSON.stringify({receipts, vendorSha256:sha},null,2)+'\\n');\nconsole.log(JSON.stringify({baseline:receipts.map(x=>({name:x.name,exit:x.exitStatus,stdout:x.stdout})),vendorSha256:sha},null,2));\n"

      "text": "# Exposed native tool binding\n\nThe session exposes collaboration.spawn_agent with task_name, message and fork_turns. fork_turns none prevents transmitting the parent rubric. Model and reasoning overrides are omitted for inherit-parent.\n\ncollaboration.followup_task targets the returned canonical worker and delivers the task. Bootstrap-only workers retain readiness state before this follow-up. collaboration.list_agents returns status. collaboration.wait_agent waits for updates. collaboration.interrupt_agent can stop active work, but was not used.\n\nfunctions.exec invokes tools.exec_command with cmd, workdir, max_output_tokens and yield_time_ms. The observed result includes exit_code, output and session_id if still running. Shell commands read files. All program scripts run with Bun auto-install disabled. No purpose-built task-list tool is exposed, so outputs/checklist.md is the reduced todo binding.\n\nThese descriptions were read from actual session tool documentation. They are not package aliases.
